druskenvald.eyebrow: The Land Between Life and Death
druskenvald.title: Druskenvald
druskenvald.quote: A self-contained demiplane where the living, dead, and everything in between can coexist.
druskenvald.body:
Druskenvald is a realm that exists outside the lands of the mortal and material. Enveloped in a seemingly endless expanse of eldritch gloom, it exists in a paradoxical state of limbo between the warring furies of life and death. Beyond the misty borders of this domain may lie countless worlds and afterlives, but Druskenvald stands apart, a self-contained demiplane where the living, dead, and everything in between can coexist.

Within these confines is a landmass hewn into the shape of a crescent moon and a dark and roiling sea that stretches from its eastern coastline until it disappears into the haze. Looming mountain peaks to the north and south flank the lands between, forming an enormous continent-sized valley that nonsensically spans numerous environments in a relatively short distance and never experiences the turn of a season. The laws of nature and logic have no dominion over a place that is just as much nightmare and folktale as it is a land to explore.

The Thirteen Provinces

The mystifying nature of Druskenvald is made most apparent by the thirteen major provinces that comprise it. As if pulled from a child's storybook featuring a broad collection of varying tales, each of these territories has a wholly distinct biome, topography, and climate. From forest to moor, desert to tundra, swamp to farmland, they all exist side by side like a collection of bizarre patches stitched together upon a grandmother's quilt. Despite the uniqueness of each Druskenvaldian patch, travel between provinces is not especially difficult, and borders can be crossed with a simple step.

Phillip & Adela Druskenvald

Since coming to power, Phillip Druskenvald has attempted to shape the realm he named after himself into a reflection of his own ideals. A master of unchained ambitions, he envisions a realm where civilization crushes the wild pulse of nature, where order reigns supreme over the primal chaos of the afterlife. In his mind, he has crafted a sanctuary, a place where souls are reborn into lives filled with the pleasures and comforts they once knew, no longer bound by the harsh cycles of nature.

In Phillip's eyes, he is a benevolent ruler who has given the inhabitants of Druskenvald a second chance at life, which he believes to be the ultimate desire of every mortal. However, as the years have gone on, he has become out of touch with the people for whom he is responsible. Often aloof and completely unaware of the realities of living in Druskenvald, he presumes that the inhabitants of Druskenvald are having as good and easy a time as he is.

At Phillip's side stands his beloved wife Adela (uh-DELL-uh), the most precious soul in existence to him. Adela was once a mortal woman living in the material world, but one born with immense powers of divination and prophecy. Her unbound curiosity, enthusiasm, and drive, along with an obsession with the spiritual world, drew her to seek out the Ghostlight Express. It is there she met Phillip, and the two fell deeply in love and were promptly married. She now assists her husband and is invaluable in the governance of Druskenvald.

The Shroud

No matter the power of the beings that dwell in Druskenvald, virtually none can pierce the wall of fog that encircles it. The phantom gloom, known among the inhabitants of Druskenvald as the Shroud, appears as a dense gray mist that wails in a chorus of agonized voices. The Shroud is, in reality, the condensed essence of the primordial element of death itself given form. It lingers just beyond the fringes of the mortal realms and serves as the veil that separates the lands of the living and the dead.

All souls not offered salvation by the hallowed or delivered damnation by the hells must pass through the Shroud on their way to the afterlife to which they are destined. They must first be led through the mist by the Strangers, timeless beings with the power to safely guide the dead to the other side. While these entities use many methods and take many forms, such as shepherds, ferrymen, reapers, or angels of death, all are bound to their solemn duty for eternity. Without the protective shield of a Stranger, the phantom mist annihilates wayward souls and devours their anima, the quintessential soul-stuff that provides all beings spiritual identity and sentience.

Rebirth & the Fate of Souls

Souls that arrive in Druskenvald are reborn into a wide variety of species, including those which inhabit the world of the living. However, the realm's predominant populace is comprised of thirteen distinct species, each having originated from one of the thirteen shrouded provinces. The origins of these species are as varied as the land itself, some rising from the landscape, others being crafted by the provincial lords, and still more arriving from magical phenomena, emerging into Druskenvald as fully formed adults, infants, or any age in between. In just as many instances, the rebirth is initiated by two parents seeking a child through biological, magical, or technological means.

No matter the species, most inhabitants of Druskenvald emerge anew, their memories of a past life erased, allowing them to live their next life with a clean slate. A few cling to fragments of their former selves, their memories either shrouded in mist or vivid and unyielding. Even rarer are those with a fully clear picture of their past life, even remembering their moment of death. While many of these beings remain in their province of origin, others choose to roam across Druskenvald and settle in other communities.

Besides the thirteen species native to Druskenvald, humans are the most populous species found in the realm compared to other folk such as dwarves, elves, or halflings. This is due to the deep connection that Phillip and Adela Druskenvald have to the domain they rule. Despite having become deathless, immortal beings long ago, their once-human hearts have left a clear imprint upon the land.

There is no guarantee of the fate that befalls those who die again while in the confines of this realm of rebirth. For many, the cycle starts once more, and the soul of the recently deceased is reborn as one of the species of Druskenvald. Sometimes, they return as the same species they had been in life, but just as often, they awaken as an entirely different one.

Some experience a "Final Death," where the soul simply fades into oblivion and ceases to exist. For those who were particularly wicked in their second chance at life, the Shroud claims it. The soul's anima is devoured, and the spirit is transformed into a shrieking abomination doomed to wander the eldritch fog forever.

crooked_moon.title: The Crooked Moon
crooked_moon.quote: In Druskenvald, the sun never rises.
crooked_moon.body:
In Druskenvald, the sun never rises. Instead, the land is bathed in an orange glow from the horizon for a few brief hours at the height of dusk, only to be swallowed by the encroaching darkness that dominates the rest of the night.

The Moon's Phases

The Crooked Moon, an eternal crescent with the visage of a leering hag, hangs eternally overhead. Its light waxes and wanes with the cycle of each night as it moves through the sky with no discernible pattern, casting long, creeping shadows. At times, it looms large in the sky, its baleful eye glowering over the land with malicious intent. At other times, it shrinks to a small sliver nearly lost in the night sky, leaving the land blanketed in total darkness.

Marking the Hours

The people of Druskenvald have adapted to their peculiar 24-hour "day" cycle from the Twilight Hour through the Witching Hour, dividing their time according to the shifting light in their own ways. Some rise as soon as the golden glow of the hidden sun shows itself above the horizon and settle in before the most treacherous hours of night. Others only wake during true darkness. While they may not agree on how to honor Druskenvald's time, all peoples and provinces have aligned on the same naming conventions for the phases of each passing night.

crescent_court.title: The Crescent Court
crescent_court.quote: Thirteen lords and ladies. Thirteen provinces. One fragile peace.
crescent_court.body:
The Druskenvalds do not rule the domain alone. There are thirteen major provinces, each with a lord or lady who governs and embodies the essence of their territory. Some of these nobles are members of the origin species of their province, while others, though different in form, still represent the province's spirit. These diverse leaders form the Crescent Court, a council that governs all of Druskenvald.

The nobles of the Crescent Court enjoy a significant degree of autonomy in the governance of their provinces with little direct oversight from Phillip. As long as each province maintains order and does not disrupt the affairs of neighboring provinces or the Druskenvalds themselves, the lords and ladies are free to rule as they see fit.

The Thirteen Lords & Ladies

The lords and ladies are as varied as the provinces they govern, some wise, some ruthless, some ancient beyond reckoning, and at least one who finds the whole affair beneath him.

  • Elder Gallows, Ardengloom
  • Headmistress Narcissa Voss, Astramar
  • Doctor Molder Underfoot, Bubonia
  • Ol' Mister Scratch, Chernabos
  • Charlotte Heady, The Iron Maiden, Edwardia
  • Methuselah, Enoch
  • Catrina the Sweet, Kalero
  • God King Xanatep, Nerukhet
  • Captain Ephraim Wake, Olmarsh
  • Archbishop Danton Alexandre Renault, Pholsense
  • Blinski II, Picco
  • Wyrm Queen Sapphira, Syndramas
  • Tazri Swampcaller, Zulrogg
Chateau Clair de Lune

Several times a year, the Crescent Court gathers at Chateau Clair de Lune (sha-TOH KLAIR-duh-LOON), the Druskenvalds' sprawling manor. The home was built by Phillip to Adela's exacting design, and it serves as an ideal place of residence and headquarters for the domain's leadership. When court is called, there is pageantry and celebration, but important matters are discussed and crucial decisions are made regarding the governance of Druskenvald.

The Coven of the Midnight Moon

Oftentimes, the primary focus of the meetings is on the malefic machinations of the Coven of the Midnight Moon. This coven of thirteen witches is led by a powerful crone known as Mother Midnight. She and her daughters work in the shadows, terrorizing the thirteen major provinces of Druskenvald to some incomprehensible end.

ghostlight_express.title: The Ghostlight Express
ghostlight_express.quote: Only the dead may see its arrival. Only the lucky reach its platform.
ghostlight_express.body:
The Ghostlight Express is the great train that carries departed souls from the mortal world into Druskenvald. It is the threshold between death and rebirth, a locomotive wreathed in spectral light that emerges from banks of dense fog with no warning and vanishes just as silently.

The Arrival

In the mortal realms, the train's arrival is heralded by the haunting sound of a fiddle and strange whistles drifting in from nowhere. The Ghostlight Express rolls in on banks of dense fog, appearing seemingly from thin air. It is said that only the dead can truly perceive its arrival, but certain living souls have discovered ways to gain passage while still breathing. Whether this is a gift or a curse depends greatly on who you ask.

The Vagrant

The Ghostlight Express is operated by a figure known only as the Vagrant, a mirthful conductor whose fiddle playing and haunting whistles announce the train's arrival. He is the shepherd of souls, ferrying the departed through the mists and into their new lives in Druskenvald. The nature of the Vagrant, whether mortal, spirit, or something else entirely, remains one of the domain's most carefully kept mysteries.

Other Strangers

The Ghostlight Express is not the only way into Druskenvald. Other mysterious figures known as Strangers have been known to guide wayward souls safely through the mists by other means. But the Express remains the most common passage, the great iron thread that stitches the world of the living to the land between life and death.

Within Druskenvald

Once inside the domain, the Express continues to operate, travelling between provinces and serving as a vital means of transport for those who can afford passage or earn it. Its competitor in Chernabos, the hellfire-fueled Devil Rail, was built specifically to challenge its dominance, though the two serve very different masters.

wickermoor_hollow.title: Wickermoor Hollow
wickermoor_hollow.quote: No records found in the archives of the Crescent Court.
wickermoor_hollow.body:
Wickermoor Hollow does not appear in any official registry of the Crescent Court. The lords and ladies of the thirteen provinces have no record of it. Cartographers who have attempted to map the valley have returned with blank parchment and troubled eyes, or have not returned at all.

What is known, or rather, what is whispered, is that somewhere between the borders of Bubonia, Enoch, and Pholsense, there is a hollow. A valley. A place where the crooked power of something old and patient settles like fog that never lifts.

Those who have been there do not speak of it freely. Those who speak of it freely have likely never been.

Locations & Lore

The details of Wickermoor Hollow are known only to those who have walked its roads. Lore is revealed through play, passwords may be discovered within the Hollow itself.

ardengloom.title: Ardengloom
ardengloom.quote: Speak not the names of the lost, for the forest has taken them. When wayward souls cross the boundary from their world to wander among the oak, ash, and thorn, they belong to the trees. Dry your eyes. The Elderwood weeps for them now.
ardengloom.body:
Ardengloom is a warning whispered by candlelight, a wood so ancient that all know its name. In a time beyond memory, the primordial forest enveloped the entirety of Druskenvald. Though now only a fraction of its former glory, its towering, gnarled trees are the last barrier between civilization and the unknown. For as long as there have been voices, songs have been sung of the terrors that lurk in the umbral heart of the wood.

The province of Ardengloom is a land of dark forests, twisting shadows, and echoes of the long-dead feyfolk who once dwelled there. Deep within the twisting roots and choking shadows lies a shrouded society. Living in remote settlements throughout the great wood, the gnarlborn are a people grown from the forest itself, resembling their treant ancestors with bark-like skin and haunting, glowing faces.

Provincial Folklore
The Ancient Elderwoods

The Elderwoods are the oldest and largest of the trees within Ardengloom. Within each of their broad trunks is a face of knotted wood and cracked bark. Should harm come to the wood in which they are rooted, they weep viscous amber sap in response to that shared pain. It is believed that within each Elderwood is the soul of a long-dead Fey, the last remnants of a once-mighty oaken empire.

The venerable language of the Elderwoods is so ancient that many folk of Ardengloom have forgotten how to speak it. Now, these primordial beings communicate the will of the woods through the subtle shifting of leaves or swaying of branches, while those attuned to the Old Ways may even hear their voices on the wind.

The Mists of Tirna Féth

On nights when the moonlight pierces through the dense canopy, a soft blue mist forms on the breeze and billows into the surrounding forests. The Mists of Tirna Féth, as they are known in legend, blanket the wood in an eerie dew, thought to be the lost souls of the feyfolk that once thrived in the glades and glens of Ardengloom.

Most who find themselves caught in the mist are trapped, forced to wander the gloom forever. The lucky few who emerge tell tales of confounding fey spirits and ghostly will-o'-wisps that may help or hinder in equal measure.

Noteworthy Folk
Elder Gallows, Lord of Ardengloom

Gnarled treants are not an uncommon sight in Ardengloom, and Elder Gallows is by far the oldest and largest of all who walk the woods. The lord of Ardengloom is so old that only the most timeworn of trees remember his true name, and none, not even the Elderwoods, dare speak it.

True to his name, nooses hang interspersed among his knotted branches as a constant reminder of the fate that will befall those who encroach upon and defile his primordial realm. Having borne witness to so much of the forest's destruction, he has become bitter toward outsiders and even his fellow lords of the Crescent Court. However, his contempt is controlled by his unmatched patience, for he knows that he and the forest will outlast them all.

Storied Locales
Gloaming Gulch

Deep within the shrouded heart of Ardengloom lies Gloaming Gulch, a flourishing city built into the very trees themselves. Spanning from the tangled roots to the towering canopy overhead, the capital is the center of society for the gnarlborn and the other species that call the forest home. Great rings of standing stones are found on the forest floor, weathered by time and enveloped by moss and lichen, it is here that the Old Ones, a group of revered treants, hold the great Gnarlmoot.

Deeply isolated from the rest of the province, Gloaming Gulch is the closest thing Ardengloom has to a city. The concept of currency is wholly foreign to those who live here. Goods are bartered at grand treetop markets, and the entire way of life is predicated on a system of honor and respect. Those who violate the laws and customs of the gulch find themselves facing merciless justice, the bones of countless trespassers are forever lost among the roots of the Elderwoods.

Maze of the Dreamers

Legends are told of a mysterious, overgrown maze built into the forest from stone, earth, branch, and bush. Marked by an archway that shimmers with emerald light, the countless miles of labyrinthian, enchanted woodland murmur with the faint song of beasts, birds, and the old gods of the forest.

Alluring song beckons unwary travelers into the Maze of the Dreamers. The lost are doomed to wander endlessly or be consumed by grasping brambles, choking ivy, or the gnashing jaws of impossibly ancient creatures within. However, it is said that those who brave the labyrinth and best its challenges will arrive at the Green Dream, the dwindled ethereal realm of the few surviving fey from the lost ages of Druskenvald.

astramar.title: Astramar
astramar.quote: Among the stars, truth is revealed. Each one is a thread that connects past, present, and future. When woven together in their multitudes, the tapestry of fate is illuminated to those with clear eyes and open minds.
astramar.body:
Astramar is a place of light in a realm shrouded in the darkness of eternal night. While the sun never rises, the glittering stars that shine down upon the towering mountains and rolling hills of the province cast it in luminant shades of blue, made even brighter by the magical ley lines that streak across its landscape. This azure brilliance illuminates not only the land and sky of Astramar but also the inquisitive and aspiring minds of the people who live there.

The harpy-like azureborn are most prominent in Astramar, descending from the night sky as they are reborn. However, the province draws all those who wish to study the arcane arts from across Druskenvald, and even beyond the Shroud.

Provincial Folklore
The Winds of Aither

In eons past, the domain now known as Astramar was the site of an impossibly powerful ritual that called down storms of arcane energy from the stars themselves. This suffused the entire province with aither, condensed arcane energy that spellcasters can draw upon to empower their magic. This volatile essence whips through the sky and crackles across the land, forming interconnected strands of power that are constantly shifting like complex wind patterns.

The people of Astramar collect the arcane substance in azure crystals embedded in the ground or held aloft in the heavens atop great towers. These crystal foci send the winds of aither across the province, fueling the enchantments, conjurations, and countless other spells that provide a wondrous life to all its inhabitants, even those born without an affinity for magic.

The Stygian Depths

In stark contrast to the illuminated landscapes of Astramar, far below its mountainous surface is a sprawling network of caverns called the Stygian Depths, where far less wondrous things lurk. The aither-touched souls of Astramar's mages are all at risk of being ripped from their bodies with one wrong incantation. When such a miscast occurs, the spirit is pulled into the underworld and joins the numerous souls that form the River Atropos, which snakes through the entirety of the Stygian Depths.

Noteworthy Folk
Headmistress Narcissa Voss, Lady of Astramar

As well as ruling the whole of Astramar, Narcissa Voss serves as the headmistress of the illustrious magical academy Gandorhal. As an azureborn, her features are owl-like, with white feathers that almost appear as spectacles framing wizened yet determined blue eyes. Voss is known among the other nobles of the Crescent Court for being especially stern, proud, and cold, but she exhibits surprising warmth and patience with all of her students.

Storied Locales
Lunarium

Astramar's grand capital is filled with ornate spires and towers that reach high into the night sky. Despite the diverse population of arcane practitioners, the city was constructed with flight-capable beings in mind, floating domes, landing platforms, and structure entrances that lead out into the clouds. Those without flight explore the city on floating arcane discs controlled by even the least magical of visitors. The Dome of Cygnus, an enormous observatory built by Lunarium's founder, houses numerous enchanted telescopes allowing stargazers from across Druskenvald to seek answers from the cosmos.

Gandorhal College of the Arcane Arts

Located on Lake Rommeda in the misty moors of Astramar, Gandorhal is Druskenvald's most prestigious magical academy. Students from across all thirteen provinces are drawn to this influential college to hone their arcane skills. The institution divides each year's class into eight houses to foster growth in each pupil's selected magical focus. The labyrinthine halls of Gandorhal are filled with mysteries and dangers that some consider unacceptable for students so young, but the professors believe that necessity is the best path to mastery.

bubonia.title: Bubonia
bubonia.quote: True power is held by those who understand that all peoples, from the rulers to the ruled, care not for any ideals and are driven solely by the instinct to survive and reproduce.
bubonia.body:
The plague-ridden province of Bubonia is bleak and shrouded in clouds of miasma and toxic haze. Amidst the instability of rampant disease and strife, rival guilds work and scheme tirelessly to achieve their individual aims. Most of the rat-like plagueborn and other species of Bubonia lead humble and often short lives, filled with constant fear. However, the guilds provide an opportunity for a life of larger purpose, excitement, and riches.

Mutant creatures, twisted by the province itself, wander on all manner of appendages and seek to destroy those still spared from their terrible fate. But perhaps even more dangerous are the plots of the province's people, where loyalty is fleeting and assassination, backstabbing, and other heinous acts of treachery are common.

Provincial Folklore
The Pestilent Haze

A sickly, yellowish-green haze hangs in the air of Bubonia, filled with plague, poison, and mutagenic power. It is from these roiling, stinking plumes that newly rebirthed plagueborn emerge. None are immune to the pestilent haze, it works slowly and insidiously, infecting the body, mind, and soul of those who breathe it. Some exhibit terrible physical symptoms and perish, while others are turned to wickedness, and still others become ravening, plagued mutants.

The best defense against the haze are huge, ancient windmills that dot the hills, built long before recorded history. However, certain schemers have discovered ways to use the windmills to harness the haze to their own unscrupulous ends.

The Five Great Guilds

While Bubonia is represented in the Crescent Court, true power resides among the many guilds. Five great guilds dominate all others:

  • The Doomsday Guild, Scientists, alchemists, and artificers who maintain power through the threat of total annihilation. Bubonia's ruling faction.
  • The Cheesemonger Guild, A union of food merchants, wealthiest of all. They trade nourishment for power, tightening their grip with each transaction.
  • The Bellringer Guild, Monks and priests who worship the pestilent haze as the Great Plagued One. They administer salves that both cure and spread the plague.
  • The Ratcatcher Guild, Assassins and spies who skitter through sewers and alleys, available for any task at the right price.
  • The Boltfinger Guild, Monster-slayers who hunt the mutants and abominations that lurk in the haze. Seemingly the noblest, but no means are too extreme.
Noteworthy Folk
Doctor Molder Underfoot, Lady of Bubonia

In a province filled with schemers, its leader must scheme best. A plagueborn who has greatly extended her life through alchemical secrets, she serves as master of the Doomsday Guild while sitting at the Crescent Court. Doomsday devices keep other guilds in line, but it is her complete understanding of minds that lets her pull the right strings to always get what she wants. Despite ruthlessness, her ultimate aim is to develop reliable immunity to the plague so Bubonia can enter a new age of prosperity.

Storied Locales
Castle Underbelly

Bubonia's capital is built into the ruins of a colossal castle abandoned before recorded history. This sprawling city is among the largest in Druskenvald, with ramshackle wooden additions grafted to ancient stone. Thousands live here, stratified by castle layers, the rich and powerful atop great towers connected by guarded walkways, the downtrodden far below in a massive sewer system. Headquarters of all five great guilds sit here, prospering from the surprising amount of trade and commerce throughout the capital.

chernabos.title: Chernabos
chernabos.quote: Fortune comes or goes with a single choice: heads or tails. But here, at least that choice is yours to make. Welcome to Chernabos!
chernabos.body:
Fiery wind howls above Chernabos and casts a strange reddish glow across its scorched wastelands and deserts dotted with ashen, skeletal remains. It is a land of extremes, blistering heat, relentless drought, violent eruptions and earthquakes, all laced with the promise of wealth beyond one's wildest dreams. Beneath fiendish volcanic peaks that belch forth ash and the imp-like ashborn, rich veins of gold and the even more valuable hell iron draw treasure hunters, opportunists, and the truly desperate from far and wide.

There is no law in Chernabos, save for what its people get away with or enforce through might, guile, or luck. Every inch of the province is tethered to the otherworldly realms of the devils, so sin itself suffuses the land, air, animals, and people with one clear ruling vice: greed.

Provincial Folklore
Hell Iron

Hell iron is a fiendish metal, pitch black and streaked with red, perfectly suited for the construction of devilish machinery that can outperform entire factories. When enormous deposits were discovered deep within the volcanic landscapes of Chernabos, there was an overnight population explosion. Enterprising folk from all over flocked to join the ashborn. Treacherous hell iron mines dot the hills, mountains, and volcanoes of the province, with the largest concentration bored throughout the hellfire-spewing Sulfur Mountain.

The Devil Rail

Built and operated by the Midas Railroad Company, the Devil Rail is an enormous train constructed from hell iron, plated in gold, and fueled by hellfire. It provides passage across the treacherous landscape of Chernabos on rails of fire and brimstone for a hefty fee of gold or hell iron. Those who board without a ticket, miss the train at the exact time of departure, or request an emergency escape from a life-threatening situation forfeit their soul, which is fed into the firebox to fuel the devilish locomotive.

Noteworthy Folk
Ol' Mister Scratch, Lord of Chernabos

A hulking devil with red skin, golden eyes, a black mustache, and curved horns, Ol' Mister Scratch maintains a cool and charming disposition despite his imposing stature. This devil takes the decrees of the Crescent Court as mere suggestions and strives to keep his province lawless, where destiny is determined with free will and the flip of a coin. Conducting his scant lordly duties from the Deadwood Theater, which also serves as a saloon, hotel, and casino, he ensures that business stays booming and greed remains king. Every soul that succumbs to sin in Chernabos becomes his.

Storied Locales
Brimstone

Brimstone, the capital of Chernabos, is a boiling cauldron of desire and desperation. Soot and smoke from chimneys mix with the sulfuric air, and its ashy streets are lined with saloons, gambling halls, theaters, and brothels a mere stone's throw from places of commerce and industry. Countless games of chance are played throughout the city, with gamblers wagering gold, hell iron, or their own souls to win jackpots beyond imagination. The signature liquor, Fiddler Johnny, is made with poisonous cactus juice and rattlesnake venom. When damnation is on the line, disputes are settled with duels to the death.

Hotel Durango

Hotel Durango isn't a myth, but it is hard to find. When someone's luck runs out in Chernabos and they lose everything, they often wander off into the desert in delirious damnation. It is to these lost souls that Hotel Durango appears: an impossibly large and remote hotel in the middle of the desert, lights inviting, door always open. Within the mirage-like hotel is everything one's heart might desire. Once a soul checks in, they leave the world they knew behind, find everything they'll ever need, and can never leave.

edwardia.title: Edwardia
edwardia.quote: The wheels of time, progress, and industry don't. We may be trapped between them, crushed beneath them, or cut down by them, but we will never be left behind.
edwardia.body:
Edwardia is a province of gray. Its sky, water, landscape, settlements, and even its people exist in a grayscale that colors every aspect of their society. The balance that its people maintain has allowed them to achieve a level of technological progress far beyond the wildest dreams of most of Druskenvald's inhabitants, sprawling cities, industrious machinery, and fantastic vehicles all powered by electricity captured from the province's frequent storms.

The wolfen curseborn emerge from the dense gray fog that rolls across the province. The society that has resulted is one obsessed with dualities, life and death, good and evil, law and anarchy, wealth and poverty, progress and regression. These opposing furies have manifested into a curse that marks every inhabitant of Edwardia.

Provincial Folklore
The Grey

Edwardia is intricately intertwined with the Grey, a term that references three parts of a whole. First, it is the name of the dense, gray fog that rolls across the province and shrouds its people in gloom for half of every night. Second, it is the name of the lifelong curse that marks every native of Edwardia, a malediction with no ongoing negative effects, but which ensures that any afflicted individual who lives a life of any extreme meets an untimely end with total certainty.

Third, this death is delivered by an entity called the Grey: a huge, gray canid beast with two heads, a she-wolf's on the left and a mastiff's on the right. Those who accept their fate are nuzzled gently by the mastiff, dying peacefully within moments. Those who flee or fight are chased down and violently torn to pieces by the she-wolf.

Sparktech

No advancement has had nearly as much impact on Edwardia as Sparktech, the revolutionary technology invented by Charlotte Heady that utilizes magnetized, bulb-shaped rods wrapped in coiled springs to capture electricity from the air. While critical to Edwardia's civilization, Sparktech is limited by its great expense, difficulty to repair, and high rate of fatal accidents. Attempts to spread the technology outside of Edwardia have failed catastrophically.

Noteworthy Folk
Charlotte Heady, The Iron Maiden, Lady of Edwardia

Charlotte Heady was once a curseborn renaissance woman who found immense passion in invention, music, dueling, and alchemy. But in the process of inventing Sparktech, a catastrophic accident annihilated her body and transmuted her soul into raw electricity. Through quick thinking, she bound her soul inside a suit of iron armor before her crackling form could dissipate. Now called the Iron Maiden, she leads Edwardia by embracing both extremes of duality in equal measure, battling the Grey with every action she takes.

Storied Locales
Baskerton

The fogbound, electric metropolis of Baskerton is the largest city in Druskenvald, with numerous high-rise buildings that pierce the gloom with bright lights and crackling tendrils of harnessed lightning. Its cobbled streets are filled with wondrous Sparktech vehicles. Statues, murals, and imagery of the two-headed Grey are displayed prominently throughout the city. Notable districts include the Progress Quarter of workshops and laboratories, Sumptown's sinister network of gang-controlled sewers and slums, The Cogs industrial district, and the spike-adorned Iron Opera House owned by Charlotte Heady herself.

enoch.title: Enoch
enoch.quote: The song of the harvest is the same as the song of the cycle of life, death, and rebirth. We all were born knowing how it goes, each one of us has a part in the harmony, and everyone will be singing it til the very end.
enoch.body:
Enoch is a rustic countryside province that sprawls across miles of rolling farmland, its fields of plenty forming a patchwork pattern across the landscape. Serving as the primary breadbasket for all of Druskenvald, it produces crops of every variety tended to by hardworking people and sold at vibrant, bustling markets across the domain. Crystal clear rivers weave through the fertile hills, delivering enchanted water to crops that allow them to grow unnaturally large.

The scarecrow-like harvestborn, crafted with care by the lord of Enoch, join in celebration with the other folk of the province to show thanks for the bountiful and relatively peaceful life afforded to them.

Provincial Folklore
The Moonlit Harvest

Despite having been driven from most of Druskenvald, primeval Green Magic hums throughout Enoch and infuses the soil, water, and air of the province with unbound growth and fertility. The knowledge of how to harness this vital power has been passed from generation to generation through story and song, providing farmers the ability to complete a full agricultural cycle every month. By the end of the month, the Moonlit Harvest is held, and all the folk of the province, young and old, head into the fields and orchards to reap the month's bounty under a brilliant moon before ending the night with a celebratory festival.

Crop Trotters

Crop trotters are giant turkeys with substantial speed, strength, and endurance that serve as the primary beasts of burden in Enoch. The province's people have a great respect and appreciation for these birds, which pull wagons, plow fields, serve as mounts, and even guard farms. For many families, they are cherished as precious pets. Each year, a great race across Enoch called the Turkey Trot is held, with folk competing to win the title of Top Trotter.

Noteworthy Folk
Methuselah, Lord of Enoch

The oldest living being in Enoch is also its leader, a black-furred cat-man with eyes as gold as the province's grain fields at harvest time. No one knows where Methuselah came from, how old he is, or how he began crafting and giving life to newly rebirthed harvestborn, but all know that if there's something to learn about Enoch, he can teach it. Wise yet sprightly, he works the fields, shares knowledge, tells tall tales, and sings songs of the harvest, it's said the crops sway to his tune.

Storied Locales
Pumpkin Hill

Atop the highest hillock, Pumpkin Hill overlooks miles of patchworked fields. Packed dirt streets wind through homes, gardens, shops, and gathering halls, converging at a lively town square where weekly markets and monthly festivals celebrate the harvest. Corn husking and pumpkin throwing contests are common, and folk dances bring joyful abandon. The Candlewick Tavern is famous for its pumpkin ale renowned across Druskenvald.

Bramblethorn Brothers' Barnstead

Barnaby, Bertram, and Bartholomew Bramblethorn run the largest and most advanced farm in Enoch. Favoring technology over tradition, they studied in Edwardia, Bubonia, and Astramar, returning with science, engineering, and alchemy to make a "modern marvel of agriculture." Their feats include week-long seed cycles, tireless harvest constructs, and modified crop trotters of great size and ferocity. Extraordinary yields come with constant side effects and mishaps, if unchecked, their Barnstead could overtake the province.

kalero.title: Kalero
kalero.quote: Moments are fleeting, just like life and love. It's the memories that remain at the end of it all… Will you join me for this dance?
kalero.body:
In Kalero, life and death are celebrated with equal exuberance. Deep canyons carved by roaring rivers dominate the land, their walls cut into settlements, roads, and innumerable tombs from which newly rebirthed relicborn emerge. These skeletal folk and others adorn themselves in vibrant colors and marigold garlands as they paint intricate murals honoring those who came before. Markets bustle and remembrance celebrations never cease.

Provincial Folklore
River of Remembrance

The River of Remembrance winds through Kalero's deep canyons like a nautical strait, shaping both land and memory. Its waters contain the lingering memories of souls lost to the Shroud. Those who peer into the current see spectral scenes of extinguished lives. The river is also a vital trade route, navigated by ships of all sizes, but plagued by sudden rapids, whirlpools, hungry river beasts, and vicious pirates lurking in hidden coves.

The Thousand Bones

Countless towering pillar-like rock formations rise across Kalero. Scaling them is near-impossible, made deadlier by violent gales and colossal vultures nesting on the spires. Yet fortune hunters try, believing golden cities and lost magical technology rest atop the bones. The secret to reaching the top is said to lie in the lost memories of Kalero's first inhabitants, hidden in a remote canyon tomb.

Noteworthy Folk
Catrina the Sweet, Lady of Kalero

A relicborn ruler who rules as she dances, vivacious and full of life that only the dead can truly savor. Her skeletal features are adorned in rainbow patterns, swirling silks, jangling jewelry, and a mane of living curls. Dismissed by rivals at their peril, Catrina pairs gregarious delight with playful cunning and fierce protection of her province's past, present, and future.

Storied Locales
Memento

Built into sheer canyon walls overlooking the River of Remembrance, Memento is a many-tiered city etched with memories and lined with altars. It never sleeps, bands play, dances whirl, shops sell flowers and sweets, and visitors flock to see the Screaming Skulls: magical fireworks that screech skyward and burst into brilliant images of the departed.

Port Melee

A protected cove houses Kalero's largest port and southern Druskenvald's center of commerce. Markets overflow with goods from every province, and rarities from beyond the Shroud. The Dorado Auction House traffics in curiosities on the black market. With riches comes constant conflict with pirates and bandits, but magical cannons that launch Screaming Skulls and a culture of martial prowess hold the line. Home to The Mastered Hand school and its elite Wave Dashers.

nerukhet.title: Nerukhet
nerukhet.quote: When doom came to the First Kingdom, we survived… In the forgotten and abandoned places of the world, we did not find this paradise waiting for us. We built it.
nerukhet.body:
Deep beneath desolate southeastern mountains and ruins lies Nerukhet, a grand underground province lit by kaleidoscopic geodes across monumental cities and webbed tunnels from which the spider-like silkborn emerge. Its people strive for greatness and divine favor, yet unrest always churns beneath, and far worse things squirm in the darkest depths.

Provincial Folklore
Tears of the Gods

Massive, sparkling gemstones, Tears of the Gods, feature prominently in Nerukhet's history. Legend says the gods wept when the First Kingdom fell, calling survivors below and gifting these gems that hum with divine vitality. They grant long life, a sharp mind, a strong body, and a sturdy constitution. Coveted and collected by the wealthiest houses, they pass down as inheritance, serve as currency, and are worn as status symbols.

The Bejeweled

Enormous, divine insects and arachnids with carapaces encrusted with jewels live in harmony with Nerukhet's people. Heralds of the gods, they share psychic bonds with families across generations. Hound-sized spiders spin the silk that clothes the province; huge locusts provide air travel; enormous scarabs build; and the rarest are dragon-sized scorpions used as symbols of divinity by powerful houses.

Noteworthy Folk
God King Xanatep, Lord of Nerukhet

Said to be the only silkborn to ascend to divinity and immortality, Xanatep rules Nerukhet, pledging only begrudging fealty to Phillip Druskenvald. He commands Vekloriash the Amethyst Dread, the largest and deadliest bejeweled scorpion, unique with great dragonfly wings. Through the Tears of the Gods, he sees across Nerukhet; few escape his gaze. His pride is unmatched, and his true aim is the greatness of Nerukhet above all else.

Storied Locales
Arakir, the Skittering City

A many-tiered, glittering capital and wonder of Druskenvald, radiant geodes, temples, tombs, palaces, and beautiful underground gardens. The Lapis Library preserves millennia of history and poetry. The infamous Tunnel of Claws houses wild, unclaimed bejeweled scorpions for those brave enough to bond with one.

The Crawling Doom

In the deepest pit lies a ruined place shrouded in legend and dread. Mighty priests sealed it with intricate spells long ago, and the details of what transpired there are not spoken of freely, even in Nerukhet. It is said that the seal weakens with each passing year, and that whatever waits in the darkness below is growing more patient, not less.

olmarsh.title: Olmarsh
olmarsh.quote: Hark, Leviathan! Hark, Albatross! … May salt foam and bilgewater forget the name of the Drowned!
olmarsh.body:
Olmarsh stretches along rocky shores and flooded salt marshes and includes numerous coastal islands. A shadow rises from below, gripping its people with fear of the unknown. Fishing sustains life beyond meager land resources, but the black ocean's threats are constant. Even the deepborn fled the depths to live on the surface, and an ever-present sense of being watched weighs from the night sky. The air is cold, viscous, and fish-stinking.

Provincial Folklore
Light of the Drowned

Eldritch storms whip up from nowhere, swallowing ships and leaving survivors babbling. The only defense against the cosmic intrusions they bring is a chain of lighthouses shining eerie ghostly light. The cost is dire, the lamps are fueled by souls lost at sea. Lone keepers tend each light, battered by incessant wails. It is an honor and a doom, their minds shatter as they grant safe passage to others.

The Hungering Ones

Colossal sea monsters are the greatest threat to Olmarsh: shelled krakens, white megalodons, fiend-whales, titanic crabs. Feared yet worshipped, they are offered food, treasure, and sacrifice in hopes of being spared. Daring crews harvest slain behemoths for Tide Ash, a valuable psychedelic found in every beast's heart. A mythical shell is said to exist that, blown like a horn, can bind a Hungering One to the blower's will.

Noteworthy Folk
Captain Ephraim Wake, Lord of Olmarsh

A renowned deepborn sailor and one of the first lighthouse keepers, Wake lasted longer than any before succumbing to the lamp's delusions. He swam to a siren, was devoured by a Hungering One, and returned the next night as a spirit bearing secrets of the deep and sight beyond the stars. Now lord of Olmarsh, he appears as a burly green ghost with a beard of tentacles and seaweed, mostly lucid, sometimes raving truths of superstitions and looming dangers.

Storied Locales
Ibbsmouth

The fog-bound coastal capital and largest port in Druskenvald. Crooked streets, gray buildings, and people who seem somehow "off." Despite the gloom, sailors and traders flock here before pursuing the supernatural bounty offshore. Eldritch relics are traded behind closed doors; chapels to the Hungering Ones are disturbingly busy. The infamous Seven Sisters tavern serves seafood stew to raucous clientele.

Darktide Manor

On treacherous cliffs at Seabird's Fall stands an impossible mansion, the headquarters of the Nautilus Order. Protected by spells, curses, marsh, and gales, it houses a museum of curiosities and a small university of the strange. Initiation requires venturing to a black reef on a night it rises and sacrificing something, or someone, precious.

pholsense.title: Pholsense
pholsense.quote: The Silver Path of the righteous is beset on all sides by the wickedness of the sinner and the heresy of the witch…
pholsense.body:
In Pholsense, life is measured by adherence to divine law. Quiet towns dot rolling hills, farmland, and woods, yet fear of straying from the Silver Path is constant. In great stone cities, built from the same rock as the gargoyle-like stoneborn, zealous militants judge and purge the wayward. Magic not of faith is distrusted; the wrong spell at the wrong time leads to a fiery fate.

Provincial Folklore
The Silver Path

More than a religion, the Silver Path is the god, an imperceivable divine will upholding five tenets: piousness, temperance, diligence, unity, and sacrifice. Zero tolerance for sin or apathy. Bells ring constantly throughout Pholsense, the faithful claim it is the god's voice. Clergy assert only they can truly interpret it, culminating in the supreme authority of the Archbishop.

The Silver Hammer

A knightly order of inquisitors and crusaders, the Silver Hammer seeks out evil as defined by the Path. Some chapters protect innocents; others use extreme, cruel methods justified as necessity. Fair trials are rare when suspicion takes root. Arcane and primal magic users are distrusted and sometimes dealt with indiscriminately, those who register and vow to serve good are tolerated or tasked to fight witchcraft with fire.

Noteworthy Folk
Archbishop Danton Alexandre Renault, Lord of Pholsense

Tall, thin, and silver-skinned with angelic eyes, Renault leads the province and church under the same five tenets. He strives for perfection, especially in his craft of carving the stoneborn, and expects it of his flock, offering forgiveness to those who confess and accept harsh penance. He delivers blistering sermons from Cyril's Cathedral of the Silver Rapture with absolute conviction.

Storied Locales
Cyril

A shining silver metropolis, one of Druskenvald's greatest, of polished stone, towering statues, and multi-tiered fountains. The Cathedral of the Silver Rapture rings dozens of colossal bells at all hours. Headquarters of the Silver Hammer and its inquisitorium's gaol, where heretics, innocent or not, are imprisoned. The Cyril Orphanage houses thousands of children. Famous catacombs sprawl beneath the city; not all visitors return.

picco.title: Picco
picco.quote: Why did Blinski build the happiest place in Druskenvald? … If Blinski can show them wonder, they might believe that change is possible.
picco.body:
In Picco, fun is law. A realm of high energy and constant motion, where real-world play thrives and wild imagination is made manifest by the master toymaker Blinski II. From his walking mechanical workshop, he creates new toys, attractions, and the doll-like threadborn, whom he loves most. To a discordant calliope, lives whirl through a fabricated landscape of cloth and props. The thrills are joyous, and often dangerous, sometimes deadly, leaving the uninitiated exhausted or terrified.

Provincial Folklore
Fun Tickets

Picco's currency is shiny carnival tickets in vibrant colors that denote different uses, food, rides, balloon travel. They power Funtopia's economy and are acquired by purchase, work, game prizes, or achieving incredible challenges. Rare tickets earned from death-defying feats hold unique magic. Collectors scour the province for them. Rumors speak of exclusive attractions and artifacts that require these rarities to access.

Jolly Jangles

Blinski mandated happiness, and created Jolly Jangles, an enormous flying cymbal monkey that guards Picco. It senses the province's mood and sniffs out negative emotions. Jolly first tries to cheer; if sadness persists, he abducts the "downers" to Blinski's workshop for "tinkering" until unbound fun is restored. The precise nature of this tinkering is not discussed in polite company.

Noteworthy Folk
Blinski II, Lord of Picco

A gregarious automaton with booming laughter and infectious cheer, Blinski II created Picco and most of its inhabitants, whom he repairs with deep affection. He travels in his walking workshop, plays with his subjects, and offers free repairs to any who need them. In a realm of night and misery, he believes it his duty to bring joy. His childlike innocence, despite great age, makes him easy to manipulate among nobles, sometimes leading to disastrous deeds done with entirely pure intent.

Storied Locales
Funtopia

The capital, equal parts carnival, amusement park, and city, runs on magical engineering. Mass-transit rides rocket commuters across themed districts:

  • Crazy Clown Hell, Hot, devilish, and packed with death-defying attractions. HQ of the Honk Legion.
  • Dinoworld, Mechanical dinosaurs amid jungle facsimiles, with a university that teaches only fun subjects.
  • Strahdanya's Castlemania, Spooky district for fun-filled frights; the Cravencroft Theater nightly stages Curse of Strahdanya.
  • Friendlyville, Wholesome fun and cozy cottages, a haven for lost and misfit toys. Mayor is a plump stuffed llama named Cream Cheese.
  • Captain Bone's Lagoon, Province-sized water park; wave pools, lazy rivers, the never-ending Captain Bone's Wild Slide.
  • Neonopolis, Music district of bright lights and cosmic paint. Much is under construction, signs promise the greatest attraction is yet to come.

syndramas.title: Syndramas
syndramas.quote: The other provinces recoil when they gaze upon the warriors of Syndramas… War makes monsters of us all.
syndramas.body:
Far to the frozen north, Syndramas is a province of perpetual battle, where the dead fight, die, and rise again to continue a war so old none recall its spark. Three warring legions scoff at peace; conflict rages across snow-bound wastes where dragon bones rest and the undead graveborn rise. Necrotic power saturates the land, anything that dies here rises as Undead to swell the legions.

Provincial Folklore
The Sepulchral Legions

Three militant legions vie eternally, each with distinct culture, tactics, and occult arts. All pledge to Wyrm Queen Sapphira, who encourages conflict within borders, total annihilation of rivals is the victory condition, and prelude to conquering Druskenvald:

  • The Rimeshade Legion, Heavily plated in drakkonite with icy, runic blades; unmatched armory, immense war machines, and floating fortresses of ancient magic.
  • The Bloodboil Legion, Total devotion and perfect synchronicity; mastery of combat through blood magic rituals granting supernatural strength and instinct.
  • The Marrowfeast Legion, Sheer numbers and viciousness; hives of dragon bone; relentless waves and vile necrotic magic that withers enemies.
Drakkonite

From the civil war that slew countless dragons, their essence leeched into the land, creating drakkonite, a dark, unnaturally cold metal. Incredibly sharp, strong, and light, it is used for weapons, armor, and structures. Drakkonite mines are hotly contested even by outsiders who risk the frozen wastes to claim it.

Noteworthy Folk
Wyrm Queen Sapphira, Lady of Syndramas

The last to die in the kingdom's brutal civil war, Sapphira's final rage sparked a necrotic chain reaction turning the province to undeath and raising her as an immense necromancer, now a skeletal dragon with desiccated gray flesh and patches of blue-white scales. She spared dragonkind from such existence; instead she raised the former humans as graveborn and rules them with pride and ruthlessness. The province's necrotic hunger has grown beyond even her control; peace is now impossible.

Storied Locales
Sepultura

An enormous fortified necropolis in the center of Syndramas, neutral ground where all legions maintain a truce within the walls and ten miles beyond. Violations are unthinkable; any who dare face Sapphira in her drakkonite citadel. Quarters are divided between the three legions and the neutral Wyrm Quarter for business with the Queensguard. Visitors are rare, but coin flows for comforts soldiers seldom otherwise know.

Dragons' End

A sacred valley graveyard of countless dragon skeletons, the site of the war's bloodiest battle. Sapphira sometimes pilgrimages here to grieve. Powerful artifacts lie scattered among the bones; would-be robbers face deadly elements, scavenging beasts, and lingering curses that have claimed many fortune hunters.

zulrogg.title: Zulrogg
zulrogg.quote: Wait. Do you hear that? It is the singing frog. It is your grandfather. It is the rain. It is the old mangrove tree. It is your mother. It is me. It is you. Look upon your reflection and listen. Will you answer?
zulrogg.body:
Despite existing in an otherworldly domain of death, the vast, tropical swamps of Zulrogg teem with life. Underneath a dense canopy of twisting, vine-choked trees, each stage of the cycle of life, death, and rebirth thrives in harmony with the others. Primal and ancestral spirits drift back and forth through the veil, offering their wisdom and guidance to those who seek it. The amphibious bogborn emerge from the mire after rebirth, forming unbreakable bonds with the bog's beasts, both natural and supernatural.

Provincial Folklore
Spirit Beasts

The province is watched over by great wild spirits that are worshipped by the people of Zulrogg. Each one takes the form of a different creature of the swamps, jungles, and shorelines and is said to possess the wisdom of all the ancestors who favored that particular spirit. Zulrogg's society is based upon the reverence of and communion with these Spirit Beasts, and making regular offerings to different spirits for different things is a fact of daily life.

This deep connection to mortals makes the spirits vulnerable, malevolent ritualists seek to capture them and siphon their essence for their own ends.

Everblooms

Countless useful flora fill Zulrogg, fueling rites, rituals, and medicine. The rarest are Everblooms, delicate flowers of pink, purple, orange, and gold, radiant with primal rebirth. They appear only in remote places at specific times and require a Spirit Beast's guidance to find. Carefully harvested petals enable master spirit priests to work miracles of healing, raise the dead, and grant immortal youth, given only to those proven worthy in the eyes of the spirits.

Noteworthy Folk
Tazri Swampcaller, Lady of Zulrogg

A bogborn spirit priest and Crescent Court member who eschews politics, Tazri leads by example and spiritual guidance. Chosen by the Hydra Spirit as its speaker, she bears many heads' worth of wisdom and is considered among the most insightful beings in all of Druskenvald. Centuries old, she extends her life with Everblooms until she finds a worthy successor. Her age seems to flicker. Eccentric and obsessed with collecting, she believes the swamp gives everything with purpose.

Storied Locales
Gurash'Atal

The largest of the stilted cities, built atop water and through trees, its wooden streets and structures connected by elaborate walkways and rope bridges. Long-necked reptilian swamp beasts ferry travelers; saber-toothed felines serve as climber-mounts. Shrines to Spirit Beasts grant blessings throughout the city. The Swampstalker Lodge displays legendary hunting trophies and teaches tracking and trapping.

Sunken Temple of Rakan'Zahl

An ancient stone temple sank beneath the swamp long ago, its dry chambers somehow intact. Those who find the hidden entrance discover ritual rooms and grottos overgrown by the bog. A cult now practices malign rites here, seeking to elevate their patron to godhood using the temple's secrets, through methods that threaten every soul in the province.

WM_BEINGS.name: Kehlenn
WM_BEINGS.flavor: The Green Queen. The voice behind the wicker. She who was here before.

WM_BEINGS.name: The Horned King
WM_BEINGS.flavor: Something is being born in the hollow. Something that has not yet been given a name.

WM_BEINGS.name: The Seven Fallen
WM_BEINGS.flavor: Seven marks on seven walls. Seven names spoken at the Witching Hour. Seven things that cannot be undone.

renathyr.name: Father Renathyr
renathyr.body: Father of the Crimson Faith and abbot of the monastery high above Dawn's Gate, a man whose sermons promise purity and salvation. Long ago he was Sir Marius, a knight-errant who swore to protect the innocent from monsters and wicked men.

farryn.name: Farryn & Gorthos
farryn.body: Farryn was a satyr of the deep Greenwood, raised in the Old Ways to tend the cycle of life, death and rebirth. Gorthos is what grief made of her.

kehlenn.name: Kehlenn
kehlenn.body: A name the hollow's oldest stories only whisper: the Green Queen, who ruled this valley before it was ever called Druskenvald.

lethica.name: Matron Lethica
lethica.body: The soft-spoken matron of Memory's Rest, pale-skinned, veiled, her cheeks streaked with ink-black tears. Once a white-haired priestess of the Nightmother, a goddess of evening, peace and healing.

crossroads.name: Mister Crossroads
crossroads.body: Mister Crossroads, as the bayou calls him: a grinning crocodile-folk dealer who will play any game, for any stake, and always knows the odds better than you do.

jericho.name: Raum & Ol' Jericho Sticks
jericho.body: Ol' Jericho Sticks, the living scarecrow who wandered Foxwillow's fields with a banjo, singing to the fieldhands. Beloved by every soul in town, until the night he vanished into the corn.

yorgrim.name: Yorgrim
yorgrim.body: A towering ghost who wanders the hollow with a great stone chained to his back, carved with the names of the clan he once failed to lay to rest.

adela.name: Adela Druskenvald
adela.body: Lady Adela Druskenvald, cheerful company and a keen reader of fortunes, who rode the Ghostlight Express beside her husband. Lately she has taken to wearing long gloves.

phillip.name: Phillip Druskenvald
phillip.body: Lord Phillip Druskenvald, master of the domain that bears his name, met travelling aboard the Ghostlight Express with his wife, Adela. Genial, assured, and rarely asked where his power came from.

tabitha.name: Tabitha Druckeryn
tabitha.body: A seamstress met at the bar of the Briar Public House in Dawn's Gate, who wants more out of life than the town seems willing to give her.

andreas.name: Andreas Maler
andreas.body: A young brother of the Crimson Monastery and son of August Maler, quietly hoping someone will help change the faith from within before it costs him his life.

august.name: August Maler
august.body: An illuminator of Dawn's Gate and father of Andreas, a widower with a sharp mind, steady hands, and a talent for drawing people in.

olaf.name: Friar Olaf
olaf.body: Friar Olaf of the Silver Bells once led the monastery, back when it was devoted to the Patient Lady. Now he lights the pyres for the Crimson Faith, and keeps a careful eye on his own skin.

cromwell.name: Inquisitor Cromwell
cromwell.body: The Crimson Faith's inquisitor: suspicious, relentless, and fond of her trophies. Few in the monastery would dare to cross her.

jaeger.name: Houndmaster Jaeger
jaeger.body: Keeper of the Crimson Monastery's hounds, whose riders and baying packs are the terror of Dawn's Gate by night.

boone.name: Vander Boone, the Bayou King
boone.body: Vander Boone, the self-declared Bayou King, who rules Murkwater Bend with thugs and taxes, and once turned down a deal with the Grinning Sinner.

lyla.name: Lyla Webb
lyla.body: The Bayou King's chief advisor, a sharp and well-connected trader who seems to know everyone worth knowing in the swamp.

vex.name: Vex
vex.body: Proprietor of a crossroads shop of potions, magical items, divination and hexes, signposted by a hand-lettered board at a fork in the swamp road.

martha.name: Martha Langtree
martha.body: A widowed farmer of Foxwillow and mother of the Langtree children, holding her family and her fields together as the town unravels around her.

jonah.name: Jonah Sawyer
jonah.body: Foxwillow's butcher, a man of long memory and longer grudges.

william.name: William Lodge
william.body: A salt-of-the-earth Foxwillow farmer with a folksy drawl and an earnest love for his failing village, who drove you to its gates.

adelaide.name: Adelaide Langtree
adelaide.body: The Langtree daughter of Foxwillow, a quiet girl who was once Ol' Jericho's dearest friend.

alda.name: Alda Farnum
alda.body: Owner of the Green Queen Inn in Wickermoor Village, all warm smiles, for whom everything is a transaction, paid in coin or in favours.

eleanor.name: Eleanor Heyling
eleanor.body: Wickermoor Village's bookseller, who will not sell a book until she has read it herself. Some say her reading has cursed her; others, that it's made her powerful.

elias.name: Elias Greaves
elias.body: A gambler, and an old friend of Adela Druskenvald, whose luck ran out aboard a riverboat in the Drowned Crossroads.

finneas.name: Finneas Trout
finneas.body: Wickermoor's bookish young schoolteacher, spectacles under a mop of brown hair, who teaches the village children their letters and holds book learning in near-reverence.

howie.name: Howie Butterman
howie.body: Deputy of Wickermoor Village, short, wiry and friendly, the affable half of the hollow's law, and quicker in a fight than he looks.

kristoff.name: Kristoff Gruber
kristoff.body: A portly, gruff regular of the Briar Public House in Dawn's Gate, whose sour manner hides a caring heart.

siv.name: Siv Harga
siv.body: Wickermoor Village's butcher, a tall, braided woman raised among the hollow's travelling herders, who took over the shop when her old master passed.

walter.name: Walter Jenkin
walter.body: A Wickermoor villager who lost his voice one night, and never quite got the whole of it back.

weston.name: Weston Murdoch
weston.body: A devout believer in the Brightsinger who welcomes any new godliness to the hollow, and who sent you looking for a missing man called Gareth.

sweetheart.name: The Sweetheart
sweetheart.body: A weeping ghost aboard the Ghostlight Express, clutching a locket with a handsome mustachioed portrait. She knows herself only as his sweetheart.

daydreamer.name: The Daydreamer
daydreamer.body: The ghost of a boy in overalls in the Dining Car, endlessly conjuring feasts and eating them, trying to swallow a guilt that won't go down.

mariner.name: The Mariner
mariner.body: The ghost of an old sailor in a sailor's coat with a clay pipe, heaving mail sacks from one end of the train to the other as if loading a ship long since sailed.

harlequin.name: The Harlequin
harlequin.body: The ghost of a jester in a belled cap, tumbling through painful pratfalls on a trapeze, her face wracked with shame.

jailbird.name: The Jailbird
jailbird.body: A ghost of the Ghostlight Express, still serving a sentence no one remembers handing down.

songstress.name: The Songstress
songstress.body: The ghost of a beautiful woman in a silky gown, smoking by the window, who dreamed of being a famous singer and never was.

vagrant.name: The Vagrant
vagrant.body: The enigmatic Stranger who guides souls into Druskenvald aboard the Ghostlight Express, the only one known to come and go from the domain as he pleases. Listen for his fiddle in the fog.

trainhopper.name: The Phantom Trainhopper
trainhopper.body: A phantom that rides the outside of the Ghostlight Express, breaking in through the windows and letting the wailing Shroud pour inside.

wm_horned_king.default:
Deep within the Wytchwood stalks a terrible beast, the manifestation of sin itself, a fledgling god of mortal desire seeking to achieve incarnation and usher in the annihilation and crooked rebirth of Druskenvald. He is the Crooked Queen's fiendish servant, and her ultimate weapon in claiming vengeance against the man who usurped her.

[[SCENE_Chapter24_Horned King]]

What Kehlenn found buried in Phillip Druskenvald's stolen power was sin itself, the darkness and desire that lurk in every mortal heart, the desperate wish not merely to survive, but to thrive and live deliciously. She held that fragment close, siphoning it slowly across centuries, weaving it into a consort and weapon born purely of wickedness.

He takes the form of an enormous black goat with three eyes the color of old blood, an incorporeal spirit bound to the haunted wood where his queen remains entombed, for now. His power spreads further than his body can reach, whispering to the frightened and the covetous throughout the hollow, offering them the life they've always wanted for the small, small price of a signature and a soul. Each name written in his book brings the Horned King one step closer to flesh, and Kehlenn one step closer to freedom.

wm_crooked_queen.default:
[[NPC_Kehlenn]]

Long before the name Druskenvald meant anything at all, this valley was a plane of Kehlenn's own making, a primordial fey goddess who ruled it as the Green Queen. Hers was an afterlife of reincarnation into pure nature, souls reborn as root and branch, bird and beast, each life brutal, short, and entirely her own to give. Then Phillip Druskenvald arrived, uninvited, and took her green and living kingdom for his own. She never learned how he found her or where he found the power to depose her, only that she was reduced to a pile of bones in a barrow and a weakened spirit bound to a single tree.

She has been waiting there ever since, biding her time and her return. As Phillip remade the domain in his image and forgot the war that unmade her, Kehlenn remembered, and her hatred for the man who stole her world never slept. Century by century she has drawn the valley's strength back into herself, calling to minions that gathered around her like moths to a flame, and the worship and twisted rituals they perform in her honor have made her stronger still, until all Wickermoor Hollow answers to her, whether its people know it or not.

[[SCENE_Chapter24_Mural]]

She calls herself the Crooked Queen now. Her servants labor toward the day she rises and takes back everything that was stolen, planning nothing short of the disintegration of every sapient being back into nature and the annihilation and crooked rebirth of the world she was robbed of.

wm_beast_of_blight.default:
Gorthos was once a satyr named Farryn, raised in the deep Greenwood to follow the Old Ways, tending the endless cycle of life, death, and rebirth alongside her kin. Her people believed attachment was unnatural, a distraction from nature's cycle, until Farryn met a human woman named Gwenna, a worshiper of the Patient Lady whose innocent idealism convinced Farryn that harmony with nature could heal even the wickedness festering in the neighboring Wytchwood.

[[SCENE_Chapter18_Gorthos]]

When Gwenna died, Farryn's grief led her to a dead primeval god rotting in the deep wood. Over many weeks she ate his decaying flesh, taking in his knowledge, his power, and his name. Each bite changed her, until the satyr was gone and only Gorthos remained. She carried Gwenna's body to the Greenwood's sacred wellspring as a final offering, and the waters spoiled, spewing forth the spores that would become the Hartsblight.

Now she wallows in heartache within her rotting den, believing that through death, decay, and an "Emerald Rebirth", a distant dream where the world returns to its pure, green state, she might see Gwenna again. Her zealous minions spread the blight in her name, every strained and sickly breath of the forest burdened by longing and the slow, relentless promise of entropy.

wm_weeping_widow.default:
Long ago, a white-haired elf named Lethica Nightborne was a high priestess of a goddess of evening, peace, and healing who takes the form of a barn owl. Her duty was to heal those sick in body or mind, achieved through blessings from her goddess and the brewing of natural remedies. She found joy in bringing peace to countless souls, but her life grew complicated when she met her husband-to-be.

After meeting the traveling knight Sir Marius Renathyr, Lethica discovered a happiness greater than she ever thought possible. Their romance was passionate, and their marriage filled her with purpose. She believed she and her chivalrous love would make the world a better place. Fate had another plan. After her husband bared his vampire fangs and attempted to feed upon her, he fled in shame. She followed him and uncovered the extent of his wickedness, shocked to learn his soul was damned and pledged to a devil. The knight she knew and loved was dead, and her new life as a widow was one of endless grief.

To ease her suffering, she redoubled her commitment to the restorative pursuit that had once brought her such comfort. She found the Isle of Mourn, drawn by stories of crystalline pools in caverns beneath the earth said to have miraculous healing powers. The legends proved true, and once she verified the water's potency, she began construction of a hospital on that very site, vowing she would bring an end to all pain. She used the waters to heal the sickly, but her own joy never returned. Hollow and bitter, she grew resentful of the goddess who failed to prevent her tragedy. Disavowing her goddess and the Nightborne name, she turned to scientific practice instead, developing more potent medicines as the hospital's construction continued.

wm_chained_reaper.default:
Yorgrim was a seer for his people before he ever set foot in Druskenvald, a shaman trusted to guide the dead of his clan to their rest. His own chieftain deceived him into performing a ritual that annihilated every soul in that clan at once, his life's single unforgivable act. He carved every one of their names into a stone, chained it to his back, and spent the remainder of his life as a wandering penitent, burying strangers' dead in place of the family he could never bury properly himself.

Death did not free him from the stone. It followed him into Druskenvald as a ghost still chained to the weight of his failure, and here he found five kindred souls as burdened as he was, a scarecrow, a knight, a pirate, a priestess, and a satyr, each carrying their own private ruin. Yorgrim softened enough to call them friends, visiting each of them in turn even as his own search for purpose continued.

That purpose found him in a cemetery built over a tear in the Shroud itself, a wound leaking centuries of furious, ravenous dead. He bound himself to the graveyard as its warden, and with fragments of his few friends' souls, he lit balefire beacons to hold the tear closed. He has held that line for longer than any mortal should be asked to. Each year the whispers on the other side of the fence grow a little louder, and Yorgrim grows a little more tired of resisting them.

[[SCENE_Chapter19_Gravedigger]]

wm_grinning_sinner.default:
Briggsy Kratch was a pirate captain once, until the sea took his crew and left him with nothing but a patron's borrowed magic to survive on. That patron was Snake Eye Jack, an ancient death spirit whose jinxcraft kept Briggsy alive long after he had any right to be. The crocodile-folk found no welcome among the swamp-folk who feared his strange magic, and the legends they spun about him grew uglier by the year. Work dried up, his schemes failed, and years of isolation and bad luck convinced Briggsy that his patron had abandoned him.

So he did what desperate men do. He rowed out to the exact point where two forgotten roads once crossed, made an offering, and summoned Snake Eye Jack himself, a many armed spirit of shadow and bone with serpents' eyes glowing neon green and pink. Briggsy challenged him to a game of dice.

They played through the whole night. Briggsy won through guile and treachery, binding Snake Eye Jack inside a hexed coffin at the bottom of the bayou and claiming the spirit's full power for himself. His body rotted like it had already been dead for weeks. His left arm withered to bone. And Mister Crossroads was born, a dealer in bargains and deals that always, always come back to get you, captain of a riverboat crewed by the souls of everyone who ever shook his hand. Every deal he strikes buys another day of keeping his old patron chained.

byGroup.1:
The house always wins, at least that's what the Grinning Sinner always thought. And he was so close. Had he claimed the souls of Adela, Tharn, Sylas, Megumin, Korrin, and Webrin, he would have fueled his boiler and kept Snake Eye Jack locked away forever.

It started to unravel in the Boiler Room. Breaking the jinxcraft loosened the grip on Snake Eye Jack's coffin prison, only a mote of light left inside the remainders of the boiler. The withered hand took the light and bolted. Before it managed to escape, you ran it down, and Sylas pinned it to the floorboards with his trusty knife. No amount of wriggling and struggling could get it free. So you gave it a chance to explain, and it was only after you'd talked to it, rather than destroyed it, that you let it go. The hand crawled back to what remained of Elias, and for one last flicker of life, the gambler stood, spoke, and offered up his own gambler's luck to Webrin and Sylas before his soul finally passed on, the hand going still and lifeless in the same moment. Megumin wasn't ready to let it stay that way. Her healing brought the hand twitching back, carrying with it whatever sliver of Elias still lingered inside.

Tharn, for his part, took to the riverboat's vices without a shred of resistance, charmed thoroughly by two lovely ladies at his table and by the games themselves. With Megumin's help, he won a hexed deck of cards off Felix Mourning, the enigmatic man you had already crossed paths with back in Wickermoor Village.

It is also whispered that he concocted a drink so foul that even the undead ferrymen behind the bar recoiled from it. It is known only as Tharn's Bramble. Gourmands stand by it, normal people fear it, but everyone agrees the name is fitting, as it always stings twice.

Sylas found something else entirely at the gambling tables: a familiar face he's kept carefully quiet about since. Whatever passed between them, it was the first peaceful conversation they'd shared, over glasses of Johnny Fiddler, their shared favorite drink.

When it finally came down to Liar's Dice with Mister Crossroads himself, you nearly lost everything before Tharn flipped the table. As the dice scattered through the air, the Grinning Sinner only smiled. But you persevered through all his tricks and put an end to the Grinning Sinner's jinxcraft for good, freeing the charmed players of the riverboat from his grip. A piece of alligator leather, a jinxed deck of cards, a handful of dice, and the thanks of the freed people serve as reminders of what happened on that riverboat.

[[SCENE_Chapter15_Dead_Mans_Hand]]

wm_harvest_terror.default:
Jericho was a haunted scarecrow, but a friendly one. He traipsed about the farmlands around Foxwillow, singing songs to drown out the sounds of sorrow within him. The people of Foxwillow loved the straw-stuffed drifter who wove through the rows of straw and stover, serenading the fieldhands on his banjo as they worked.

But eventually, even music was not enough to resist the voice inside his head. As the decades passed, the demon that Jericho called "Virgil" grew in power and slowly spread his discord to the people of Foxwillow. The townsfolk grew more suspicious of him, filling the scarecrow with increasing self-doubt, and Virgil preyed on that uncertainty, manipulating his wounded psyche until Jericho gave in to the whispers. When Jericho realized the demon inside him was gaining control, he retreated into the cornfields to keep his beloved Foxwillowers safe. Tragically, the struggle was short. His soul was devoured by Virgil, and the two merged into a new demon in the crumpled scarecrow body. He is now Raum, the Harvest Terror, a crow-like fiend with a body of straw and rusted metal.

byGroup.1:
This fiend corrupted and sowed dissent into Foxwillow, which piqued the interest of a few spiders. One of them was bold enough to take an even closer look. So it happened that into the cornrows four entered, and five emerged. Only you know what happened in the field, and whether the experience strengthened your bond or frayed the threads of trust even further. But that is only for you to know, as this secret is the one you are allowed to keep.

[[SCENE_Chapter13_Harvest_Terror]]

wm_crimson_abbot.default:
Sir Marius Renathyr was once a knight-errant of another world, his armor gleaming gold, his banner a lionhearted red. Cast into the fallen land of Druskenvald by means unknown, his conviction toward righteousness never wavered, and he gathered knights to his side to protect the innocent from monsters and wicked men. One such innocent was a traveling priestess named Lethica Nightborne, devotee to a goddess of sheltering night called the Nightmother. He rescued her from cruel men on the road and delivered her safely to her cloister, and love blossomed between the knight of light and the priestess of darkness. Marius remained chaste and returned to his questing, but his visits to the cloister grew frequent as their love burned, even as the years and his sacred mission dulled his kindness into zeal, and his zeal into wrath.

That wrath drew the attention of a devil named Viraxys, who fed on mortals corrupted by their own evil impulses and saw in Marius a puppet worth making. She set a small army of bandits against him, left him near death, and offered false salvation: immortality, in exchange for his blood and his service. Marius accepted and rose again as a vampire, his knightly sword transformed into a blood-soaked blade, a mark of his new and terrible allegiance. He returned to his wife and confessed what he'd become. Though Lethica loved him still, his shame blinded him to her devotion, and bloodthirst nearly claimed her when he lost control in a single terrible moment. He regained himself just in time, but the guilt was more than he could carry, and he abandoned her, wandering until he reached the town of Dawn's Gate.

[[SCENE_Chapter14_Renathyr]]
