There, Viraxys led him to a small monastery, where his knightly charm and his zeal, now bent toward her false goddess the Crimson Rose, corrupted the monks into followers. Four years passed before Lethica found him again, no longer her husband but Father Renathyr, fanatical leader of the Crimson Faith. Horrified by what he'd become, she fled to the Isle of Mourn.

[[BOSS_Crimson_Abbot_Transformed]]

byGroup.1:
And he saw great power and potential in them, but with great power and potential comes great danger and threat. But what is the Crimson Rose if not welcoming and nurturing? So he invited them to the monastery, gave them shelter, and fed them. Even knowing their true reason for coming, he still held hope for them.

He was not truly surprised when he met them in the Sanctum. He had thought he would persuade them there, but instead they showed him what he had known for a long time but refused to accept: he had become the very thing he once swore to destroy.

Seeing in them what he once was, he wished only for one thing, to die a knight's death.

In the fight that followed, as Renathyr's zeal twisted him into something monstrous, he commanded Tharn to kneel. But as Tharn looked into the Abbot's eyes, he felt, just for a moment, something other than fury there, and Renathyr's blade came down not into him, but into the stone beside him.

[[BOSS_Crimson_Abbot_Transformed]]

wm_hartsblight.default:
Hartsblight Forest was once a lush and verdant woodland at the edge of Wickermoor Hollow known as the Greenwood, home to a community of antlered, deerlike satyrs who cared for its flora and fauna. Now it is a rotten place, putrefied by Hartsblight, a fungal infection that brings decay to all living things.

[[SCENE_Chapter18_Hartsblight]]

The trees here have gone the color of old bruises, and the air carries a wet, sweetish stink that clings to clothes and hair long after leaving. Fungal blooms crust over bark and stone alike, pulsing faintly as though something beneath them still breathes. Animals that wander too deep don't come back out, or come back out wrong, hollow-eyed and rotting on their feet but still somehow walking. The locals blame a fallen satyr for the corruption, and they are not wrong to.

[[Hartsblight Forest]]

wm_wytchwood.default:
No road leads into the Wytchwood, and none leads back out. It is the oldest wood in the whole of the hollow, wild since before the hollow had a name, and it does not forgive visitors. There are no paths beneath its sixty-foot canopy, only the trails beasts make and unmake as they please, and the needled branches overhead swallow sound so thoroughly that a shout carries no farther than a few hundred feet before the forest simply eats it.

[[SCENE_Chapter24_Wytchwood]]

Those who wander far enough in report the same strange details: a sense of being watched from just beyond the treeline, belongings rearranged in their camp by morning with no memory of who moved them, and if they are unlucky, or unlucky enough to be looking for it, a huge shape moving parallel to their path in the dark, three red eyes catching what little light the Crooked Moon lets through the canopy. Somewhere at the center of it all is a single crooked tree, ancient beyond telling, and everyone in the hollow who has ever gone looking for it has understood, eventually, why no one ever comes back.

wm_drowned.default:
The lowest point in the whole of Wickermoor Hollow is a black-water swamp of standing pools and choking overgrowth, and it was not always the way it is now. Years ago, fortune came easily here, gold flowed freely and luck seemed to favor everyone who tried their hand, and word spread until people came from across the valley hoping the swamp would be kind to them too. It was, for a while.

Now the swamp is jinxed, and the people who live here aren't wrong to say so. Accidents, sickness, and financial ruin have all become far too common, with no end to the bad luck in sight. Worse, the hex has brought the Drowned Crossroads to a kind of unnatural life. The mire itself has been known to rise up and drag the unwary down into its murky depths. In the Midnight Hour, faint brass music drifts through the gloom, and somewhere out past the reach of any lantern, the running lights of a riverboat drift closer and never quite arrive.

byGroup.1:
[[Drowned Crossroads]]

Need a Hand?

The ground grew sodden and foul-smelling underfoot, and before you rose a looming wall of cypress and tupelo, branches reaching out like skeletal fingers over long shadows and murky, stagnant water. This was the Drowned Crossroads, and it did not welcome you kindly.

A nest of Bayou Beasts rose out of the mire before you'd gone far and attacked. In the aftermath, a severed hand crawled into your camp uninvited. It cannot speak, only twitch and gesture, but whatever it wanted, it wanted badly enough to follow you the rest of the way, and you let it.

Crooked Fortune

Further down the trail you came across a small exchange stand, and past it, a fork in the road with a hand-lettered sign pointing right: Vex's Potions, Magical Items, Divination and Hexes. You chose not to follow it, not that day. At the stand itself, you traded a jinxed poker chip for a vinyl record salvaged from the Ghostlight Express, and half a bottle of moonshine for a bottle of jinxed rum. Ever since, luck has had a strange habit of bending around Sylas and Tharn in particular, for better or worse. Not long after, a black cat began watching you from the treeline, keeping just far enough away to avoid a clear look. What it wanted, or who sent it, nobody figured out then.

Vex's Hexes

It would be many miles and many dangers later, on the road back out of the swamp, that curiosity finally won out and you followed that sign to its end: a witch's hut standing on frog legs in the middle of a lake, the croaking of unseen frogs never quite stopping. Vex, the hagling who called it home, and the black cat's true mistress, proved a shrewd businesswoman, giving away only exactly as much as a price could buy. She taught you how to call your familiars back should misfortune claim them, in exchange for a chalice of dried blood, a deal whose fairness is still up for debate. Impressed by what she saw in you, she offered a second bargain: bring her the right magical ingredients, and she would craft an enchanted item for each of you in return.

Alligator's Smile

You had been warned before you set out: don't bring horses into the Drowned Crossroads. You found out why the hard way when a nest of alligators rose from the black water, and horses or no horses, it nearly turned into a eulogy.

Moonshine

It was in the calm after that a wandering spirit calling itself Moonshine found you around a campfire, hungry for stories. After a long night of trading tales, it decided to stick around, curious to see how your story would end.

And Stay Dead.

The last fight before Murkwater Bend was no contest at all. Whatever undead the swamp threw at you that night, you tore through without slowing down, and you walked the rest of the way to the stilt-town without looking back.

wm_howlers.default:
The mountains that wall off the western edge of Wickermoor Hollow take their name from the wind that never stops moving through their peaks, a constant, mournful howl that the people below have long since stopped hearing as unusual. Snow crowns the summits year-round, and the range stands as close to an impassable border as anything in the hollow gets, cutting the valley off from whatever lies beyond it just as thoroughly as the Shroud does everywhere else.

Dawn's Gate clings to the foothills, its people scraping a living from hunting, farming and mining the lower slopes. It was founded on hope once, a belief that the Patient Lady might someday deliver sunlight to Wickermoor Hollow, but that hope withered generations ago along with the founders who carried it. What fills the space it left behind is enforced with unwavering severity, and every night, the bell calls the village to prayer whether its people feel like praying or not.

wm_moonsong.default:
The Silverbell River runs its whole course to empty here, into a lake so wide it looks more like an inland sea, and the weather over Moonsong Lake seems to know it, rain falls here more often than anywhere else in the hollow, sometimes for weeks without a break, until the shoreline turns to standing mud and the water takes on a permanent, silvered gloom.

At the center of the lake sits the Isle of Mourn, reachable only by boat and only if you know which boatman to ask. It was once spoken of as a place of healing, and in a sense it still is, crystalline pools beneath the island are supposed to mend anything. What isn't spoken of as freely is why so few of the patients ferried out to the island's sanatorium are ever ferried back.

[[MONSTER_Lake_Dredger]]

byGroup.1:
A single wooden rowboat waited for you on the shore, and the few hours it would take to cross to the island should have been almost peaceful, rain on silvered water, nothing but the creak of oarlocks to break the quiet. It would have been, if not for the Lake Dredger, a bloated, long-necked horror rotting beneath the kelp, the kind of shape old sailors used to swear they'd seen and nobody believed.

It came up fast and without warning, and the fight that followed was brutal enough that both sides eventually broke off to nurse their wounds rather than see it through. Tharn came closest to not walking away from it at all, swallowed whole in one snapping bite, and had to cut and claw his way out through the creature's ribcage from the inside just to breathe air again.

[[MONSTER_Lake_Dredger]]

wm_memorys_rest.default:
From the outside, Memory's Rest looks exactly like what its name promises: a quiet sanatorium on a quiet island, offering rest to anyone whose grief has grown too heavy to carry alone. Its founder, a soft-spoken matron with pale skin and ink-black tears, greets every new patient personally, and her staff are unfailingly gentle. Behind the iron doors, the halls are a great deal less peaceful than the waiting room suggests.

[[SCENE_Chapter17_Memorys_Rest]]

byGroup.1:
[[Memorys Rest]]

Within the sanatorium's walls, you were met with calm and violet light. Masked nurses greeted you at reception, and before long you were ushered into the Matron's office. She entered without a sound, almost as if gliding above the floor, and not even the door dared to creak.

Inky tears stained her face, her eyes hidden behind a veil, as she welcomed you in. For just a moment her composure slipped when you mentioned Marius Renathyr, and she made it plain she wished to hear his name no further. You pushed anyway, driving the thorn deeper into a wound that had never healed, until she demanded you leave. It was a bold move, reckless even, but it bought you more than you expected, and more still once Webrin took matters into her own hands, scaling the sanatorium walls to peer in through its windows from outside.

What she saw there was never meant for her eyes. Men in doctors' clothes, if doctors was truly the word for them, cutting open a patient's chest, and if the screams hadn't already told her enough, the wriggling movement beneath their clothes made it clear something truly wicked had taken root in this so-called place of healing. Her spying didn't last. The surgeons noticed her and raised the alarm, sending nurses and orderlies pouring out of the sanatorium to escort, or pacify, the unruly visitors by whatever means necessary. You made the choice to leave.

For now.

wm_skitterdeep.default:
Seventy years ago this was Glitterdeep Mine, and its veins of gold, silver, and iron made it one of the richest sites in the valley, until a cave-in swallowed fifty men in a single night and nothing was ever quite the same. The knights who went in after them came back speaking of centipedes the size of hounds pouring down out of the tunnel walls, and then they stopped coming back at all. The mine was condemned. Most people pretend it was never anything else.

[[Skitterdeep Mine]]

It wasn't a cave-in. A centipede hag named Stonoga Blackstinger, middle sister of the Vermintoll Coven, had already wormed her way into the miners' trust with illusion, hearty food, and stronger drink, long before the tunnels ever came down. Once she had that trust, she had everything else, and she poisoned and twisted every last one of them into grotesque abominations before collapsing the mine to keep them buried and hers. The knights sent to rescue them fared no better, warped into new minions the moment they set foot inside.

Skitterdeep, as the tunnels are called now, still spreads. The centipedes are only the part you can see. Stonoga's influence has crept beneath the earth for miles, and it has been a very long time since anyone in Wickermoor Village could say with total confidence what's crawling under their floorboards at night.

wm_village.default:
Wickermoor Village is the oldest settlement in the hollow it's named for, a small, timber-framed town built around a circular square known as the Founder's Round. On one side stands a ten-foot granite statue of a nameless founder, its face and details worn smooth by time until no one living remembers who it depicts. Across from it grows the Oak of Many Faces, ancient and gnarled, its bark carved over with what must be hundreds of faces, one for every soul the village has offered up before it over the years.

[[SCENE_Chapter11_Wickermoor_Village]]

The people here have survived for centuries by heeding nature in its bounty and its wrath, and their certainty in the Old Ways has never wavered, no matter how strange, violent, or unexplainable the happenings around them grow. They are, on the surface, a welcoming folk, quick to open their doors to strangers passing through. What they rarely say aloud is how badly they want those strangers to stay, and to believe.

byGroup.1:
Arrival

On arrival, you were met with a grim welcome: a human-sized doll staked to the ground before the Oak of Many Faces, a baby goat sewn inside it, struggling to break free, while a pack of wolves closed in from across the square. You chose to let the ritual play out and let the wolves have the goatling.

[[Wickermoor Village]]

A Stone Finger

Beyond the ritual at the Founder's Round, you looked into a stranger death: a man found dead in the square itself, clutching a stone finger in his hand. The investigation turned up nothing conclusive in the end, though it left you with a hunch you haven't let go of.

Bad Seed

Later, the village held a harvest festival, tables heavy with baked goods and treats of every kind, until the celebration soured. Several people fell suddenly ill, veins blackening beneath their skin as though some curse had taken hold. With your investigative instincts and Deputy Howie Butterman's help, you traced it back to cursed apples from a nearby orchard.

You found the orchard beautiful despite it all, a single giant tree standing at its heart, and in the house nearby, an old woman who tended it alone. You pressed her, firmly but not unkindly, and learned that a man with crooked limbs had given her the apple sapling years before. She let slip the tree's one weakness: offer it fruit of its own, and it would weaken. Armed with that, you moved against it. The tree very nearly killed Howie Butterman before it fell, but fall it did, and Megumin took a sapling from beneath its roots before you left.

Year Walk

[[Winter Tale]]

When you returned from Foxwillow, the first snow of the year had begun to fall over the Hollow. The village transformed around it, children rehearsing carols, villagers raising stalls in the square. Ever curious, Korrin sought out Eleanor and learned what was coming: the New Year, and with it, the chance for a Year Walk, a ritual promising a great boon and an equally great cost to those who failed it. The rules were simple and unforgiving. Enter the forest with no food, speak not a single word, reach the chapel deep within, circle it three times, and look through its keyhole to glimpse the future. Above all, do not be tricked by whatever the forest sends to greet you, for that would mean ruin.

You did not have to wait long to see them. Great furred shapes moved through the snow, masked, horned, hung with sleighing bells, and the villagers knew without being told which ones to approach and which to avoid. Once the Perchten had passed, a horse skull came next, moving door to door through the village, trading rhymes with whoever answered, taking a prize from anyone who lost the exchange. Megumin, after some arguing with Alda, took up the challenge herself, matching Mari rhyme for rhyme and wit for wit, and won.

The feast that followed was full of song, until panic crept in beneath it. Mothers began calling into the streets for children who answered only with silence and snow. It became clear soon enough that Mari's prize that year had not been limited to food and drink. Search parties formed fast, and you took the most dangerous ground, the forest itself.

It was bitterly cold in the trees, the wind cutting all the way to the bone. First came the Night Raven, demanding payment in blood, warmth, and memory. Then came children, though not the ones you were searching for, mylings that clung to you and made every step heavier than the last. A brook horse offered a ride, and Sylas took it, only for the horse to leap with him straight into the icy river below, a plunge that nearly killed him but forged a bond between them all the same. Further on, a band of mice showed you the way forward.

In a small glade, you found a woman cooking stew over a fire, inviting you to sit, warm yourselves, and eat your fill. It was enticing enough that you did, but something about her wouldn't sit right, no matter how you reasoned with it. You chose to press on into the forest instead, and it was the right choice. The fire had no warmth in it. The food would never have filled you. Had Korrin's tiredness taken hold of the rest of you the way it nearly did him, you would still be sitting frozen in that glade to this day, because a Huldra does not let go of what she's caught.

Deeper in, the thicket grew worse, until one of the trees itself moved, a Leshy stepping into your path, judge and jury both. He would let you pass unharmed, but only on one condition: Tharn, in whom he saw a kindred spirit, had to strike a bargain with him. Tharn agreed, and the thicket opened.

Beyond it stood a chapel behind a low stone wall, a cemetery within, a Grim keeping watch over the gate. The mylings found their proper rest there at last, free to cross to whatever waited on the other side, and you found your own way in, and your path to the keyhole that showed the future. Eleanor was waiting inside, relieved to see familiar faces, and you rested a while to gather your strength before facing the heart of the storm.

Mari Lwyd's true form was worse than the skull you'd seen in the village, a horse's skull on an impossibly long, crooked, coiling neck of bone. But she fell, and the missing children were saved, however lasting a victory that can be against a spirit like her.

With the children home safe, you returned to a village that hailed you as heroes, and the feast carried on long into the night, now sung in your name.

Cat Got Your Tongue?

[[MONSTER_Ketgrin]]

When you arrived back in Wickermoor, Finneas, or rather his voice, coming from behind a closed door, urged Sylas to meet him by the tree at the Midnight Hour. It was a ruse from the start, the work of a Ketgrinn calling itself Wisp, a voice-thief that had already taken Walter Jenkin's voice a month prior, then Finneas's, and now had its sights set on Sylas's. Neither the tree's aid nor Wisp's attempt to lure Sylas out alone was enough to claim it. Sylas turned the tables instead, taking its life rather than losing his voice, silencing it for good.

Or so it seemed. Meow.

Cursed is the Winner

A lottery came to town, run by an enigmatic man named Felix Mourning, dressed head to toe in black, a wide-brimmed hat and bolo tie completing the look. He drew in nearly the whole village with the promise of a priceless magical artifact, one said to shield its wearer from all bad luck and draw all good fortune toward them instead. The price of entry was nothing more than a handshake, a name written on a card, and three copper pieces. You entered alongside everyone else, Sylas included, though Sylas wrote down a name that wasn't his own, some instinct warning him there was a trick buried in the offer.

Perhaps that instinct is exactly why he won. The item was every bit as powerful as promised, but its gift came with a cruel trade, every scrap of good luck it gave its wearer, it stripped from everyone standing near them, redirected as bad luck instead. Sylas didn't keep it long. He gave it away to a young boy in town, and what he meant by that, or whether it was even a kindness, is hard to say. But for a while at least, the boy and his mother found a little peace they hadn't had before.
byGroup.2:
Arrival

On arrival, you were met with a grim welcome: a human-sized doll staked to the ground before the Oak of Many Faces, a baby goat sewn inside it, struggling to break free, while a pack of wolves closed in from across the square. You chose to let the ritual play out and let the wolves have the goatling.

[[Wickermoor Village]]

Play is a Deadly Thing

[[Pyemethers Place]]

Since the encounter in the Crooked House, strange happenings have followed you through the town. Things fell and broke without explanation, and a light trailed you through the streets at odd hours. Odd as it was, it wasn't without its uses, a signpost came loose and struck Randal square on the head, leaving him too dazed to stop you from slipping through his barbershop and down the hatch into his cellar. There you found what he kept hidden below: teeth, hair, and blood, cast-offs and leftovers from his customers, saved for use in Old Ways rituals. Randal himself was in no state to answer questions about any of it, and the light that had led you there wasn't finished either, it kept pulling you onward, toward a boarded-up house on the edge of town.

You could smell a trap before you ever reached the door, so you turned back to prepare instead, setting your sights on the coming trip to Foxwillow. One of your stops along the way was the antiquarian's, searching for books that might help you understand the world closing in around you. Two such books, it turned out, had been checked out long ago and never returned, last signed for by the Pyemethers. That thread led you right back to the boarded-up house, still and waiting, until the door creaked open on its own and a light appeared, deep in the back of the building.

Your unease was well earned. The moment you stepped inside, the door slammed shut behind you, and the rooms themselves began to shift and rearrange, the house's true master finally free to play with its newest guests, a lantern-eyed thing called the Kackle. But you weren't the kind of prey the Kackle was used to, children and villagers who never fought back, and the hunt turned around on it fast. You fought your way to its lantern and smashed it, ending the Kackle for good.

That should have been the end of it. Instead, something worse woke up in its place, and the house itself turned against you, walls and halls twisting to keep you from ever finding the door again. You escaped by the skin of your necks, Ash coming closest of all to becoming a permanent resident. But escape you did, books in hand, carrying more questions out of that house than you'd carried in.

That evening, worn thin from the whole ordeal, only a few of you had the energy left to watch the traveling theater troupe's performance: The Tragedy of Farryn of the Greenwood.

[[SCENE_Tragedy_of_Farryn]]

Familiar Faces

Wickermoor was much as you had left it. The barber, the schoolteacher {{npc:finneas|Finneas}}, {{npc:phillip|Lord}} and {{npc:adela|Lady Druskenvald}}, and the town's poor madman, left in peace for once. After everything in Foxwillow, a night's rest at the inn felt well earned.

Children of the Green Queen

It did not stay restful for long. Rumours were going round of something that only happens once in many years: children slipping from their beds at night and walking into the forest, coming home the next day ravenous. The villagers whispered that the children had been chosen, that the Green Queen was calling them, and that those she chose would be sent away to live with her.

Asking around turned up eight of them, though not every parent would admit it; some flatly denied their child had anything to do with it. The eldest was Marta, a thirteen-year-old orphan.

The Circle in the Woods

You waited for nightfall, and when one of the girls rose from her bed, you followed. She led you deep into the forest to a moonlit clearing where the children stood hand in hand in a silent circle, and they were not alone. The village apothecary was there, watching over them.

She told you the truth of it. The children were carrying a fungus, and this was how it spread: a natural cycle, nothing more, that would pass with time. She knew, because she had walked into these woods herself as a child. The Green Queen had nothing to do with it. The real cruelty lay in what the village did afterwards, sending every child who walked away into exile, as if something ancient had claimed them.

Grist, for once, looked satisfied. Here at last was something real, something that could be measured, and while the others comforted the children, he gathered his samples.

Home by Morning

When morning broke the spell, you gathered all eight children, Marta among them, and brought every one of them home. Then came the harder part: convincing the village. Armed with what the apothecary had told you, you went to the people who mattered, the mayor among them, and with {{npc:adela|Lady Druskenvald}}'s help you finally had enough weight behind you. The children would be welcomed home once their nights of walking were over, not cast out into the woods.

Marta did not stay behind. The orphan girl was placed in your care, and Tihana took her under her wing at once, determined that she would grow up strong, confident and free to choose her own way. Tihana had changed too. Somewhere between Kalero and here, the cleric of the Harvest had set aside her holy symbol and taken up the blade. Her resolve to protect others had not faded; it had simply found a new shape.

Feathers and Ashes

Not every face in Wickermoor was a friendly one. At the pigeon coop you caught sight of a figure from Astramar, one of those sent to bring Tihana home, who fled before you could reach him. Ash went inside after him and found a letter addressed to himself, burned almost entirely to ash.

Word from the Monastery

Then a priest brought news from the mountains: the Crimson Monastery had fallen into turmoil, and violence had broken loose within its walls. Basaltos, ever hungry for justice against the wicked, would not hear of staying away, and the rest of you agreed. The road there crosses the Silverbell River and runs for several days on foot.

The Ruined Temple

Before setting out, you stopped at a ruined temple in the village that was being rebuilt. Its old carvings belonged to the Silver Path, though a new faith was overseeing the restoration. Among the ruins Basaltos heard a voice that no one else did, and he left with a sense of where his own answers might be found.
byGroup.3:
Arrival

On arrival, you were met with a grim welcome: a human-sized doll staked to the ground before the Oak of Many Faces, a baby goat sewn inside it, struggling to break free, while a pack of wolves closed in from across the square. Brzik spoke with the wolves, and found them bloodthirsty, yes, but not truly aggressive toward him. The pack's leader went so far as to offer him a place among them, should he ever want it. You chose to let the ritual play out and let the wolves have the goatling.

wm_foxwillow.default:
East of the village, the land opens into miles of fertile farmland that once fed the whole of Wickermoor Hollow, golden fields, tidy homesteads, a community that took pride in what it grew and who it fed. They worship the Patient Lady here, friendly, hardworking folk who help their neighbors and never speak ill of anyone, not to their face, at least. A friendly scarecrow named Ol' Jericho Sticks used to wander these fields with a banjo slung over his shoulder, singing to the fieldhands as they worked, beloved by every soul in town.

Then, six months ago, Jericho vanished into the corn without a trace, and Foxwillow has been unraveling ever since. Suspicion came first, neighbors certain other neighbors knew more than they were saying, old grudges dragged back into daylight and left to fester. The crops began failing not long after, everything but the corn to the east, insects swarmed, cattle wasted and died, and still the town found ways to blame each other rather than whatever was actually happening around them. Worse came later still. Townsfolk started disappearing outright, replaced by grotesque, pumpkin-headed scarecrows propped in their homes and shops as if nothing had changed. Now murders of crows gather thick enough in the bare branches to make the trees look full again, watching, always watching, on behalf of whatever waits for the town out in the corn.

byGroup.1:
[[SCENE_Chapter13_Foxwillow]]

Fire in Foxwillow

The trip to Foxwillow started calm, a welcome chance to digest everything that had happened over the past few days and finally catch up on sleep. That calm vanished as fast as the smoke rising over the town ahead of you. Foxwillow, the place you'd come to help, was burning. There was no time to waste. William spurred the horses to a sprint and got you to the village square, where chaos was already in full swing, scarecrows fighting each other in the streets, the general store and town hall both ablaze, and behind it all, the windmill's burning sails throwing sparks in every direction.

You got to work fast, hauling water to the store and the town hall, but the effort drew the scarecrows' attention, and a fight broke out. It nearly ended the adventure then and there. Tharn was driven back from the very brink of death by some force even he couldn't name, and together you finished what the scarecrows started, tearing several of them apart completely.

What the Windmill Held

With the fires under control, you turned to the windmill, first freeing Martha, then Jonah and his scarecrow daughter alongside him. The moment Martha apologized to Jonah, as if the words themselves cut the last thread holding the fight in them, every scarecrow around you went still. The town was well and truly empty after that, only three people left breathing in all of Foxwillow, not counting the scarecrows that still stood watch over everything.

Secrets Uncovered

[[SCENE_Chapter13_Windmill_Cellar]]

True to form, you combed the town for every clue and scrap of information you could find, and you found plenty. Isaac, Martha's son, lay dead in the windmill's cellar, most likely killed by his own sister Adelaide. You brought the news to Martha, but a mother who has already lost one child doesn't need the wound dug any deeper, so you kept Adelaide's part in it to yourselves, the way everyone in this town seems to keep something to themselves. Jonah the butcher had his own secret, a ritual he'd used to curse William's animals and crops, out of nothing more than spite over William selling his better livestock to Siv in Wickermoor. And in the wreckage, three small trinkets turned up: a banjo, a certificate of citizenship, and a sheet of music, gifts the town had once meant to give Jericho, to show him just how loved he really was.

With the town's secrets in hand, and Jericho's trinkets besides, you were as ready as you'd ever be to step into the Fields of the Crow.

[[Fields of the Crow]]

The Last Song

With Raum defeated, the spirits of the missing returned from the fields to their bodies, carried home on one last song from Jericho. The dead were mourned properly, and a feast was held in your names. Out of it came a decision the whole town seemed to share, that there would never be another secret kept in Foxwillow.

[[SCENE_Chapter13_Goodbyes]]

Passing Through Again

On the road to the Drowned Crossroads, you found yourselves passing back through Foxwillow's fields and town once more. Along the way you helped a witchwoven trying to impress the one he loved, blessing his journey before continuing on your own. The town itself felt different this time, as if some heavy blanket had finally been lifted from it, people hard at work again, and the followers of the Patient Lady doing what they could to root out whatever curse still lingered in the soil. The stop was brief, though Webrin, for one, wished it could have lasted longer.

The fields beyond town were unremarkable by comparison, save for a chance encounter with a stray dog and a moment where Webrin caught something watching you from between the rows. There was no time to look closer this time. A case had already been placed in your hands, and by hells, you were going to solve it.
byGroup.2:
Into the Corn

[[SCENE_Chapter13_Foxwillow]]

Foxwillow offered you a reward to find its missing people, and the trail led where every trail in that town seemed to lead: into the corn. The fields had become a labyrinth, rows shifting and closing behind you, and somewhere at its heart lay the curse that had turned the townsfolk into scarecrows.

Doubt came easily in there, the fear of failing and of every soul in Foxwillow being lost to whatever waited in the middle. But a silver path ran through the maze, and following it was the only way forward. Basaltos held fast to his faith, and his steadiness kept the rest of you moving.

[[Fields of the Crow]]

Monstrous crows found you among the stalks, {{creature:corvodaemon|corvodaemons}} reeking of carrion, and they either fell to Basaltos's smiting or fled. You sang as you went, a new song that steadied your nerves and seemed to hold the dark at bay, and spirits began to gather along the way, drawn to it.

The Thing in the Clearing

At what looked like a dead end, the corn opened onto a clearing. A Harvestborn stood in it, his face twisted and his mind plainly not his own, and then something tore its way out of him: a towering crow demon with a cage where its chest should be and a scythe for a hand, wrapped in a storm of crows and whispering into every one of your minds at once.

[[SCENE_Chapter13_Harvest_Terror]]

The fight was brutal. The scythe rang off Basaltos's shield and cut through armour to skin, the demon called minions to its side and raised walls of howling wind, and for a while it was far from certain who would walk out of that field. Faith and sheer stubbornness carried you through, and {{creature:harvest_terror|the Harvest Terror}} fell. It left strange tools behind. Basaltos would not so much as look at them; some of you kept them anyway.

Foxwillow Restored

You came back out of the corn with company, several of the spirits having attached themselves to you, unwilling to rest until something was settled. Foxwillow was not the town you had left. Those who had been scarecrows were people again, all but a few unlucky souls, and you helped those last few find their peace by carrying the words they had never said to the people they had left behind.

[[SCENE_Chapter13_Goodbyes]]

Foxwillow threw you a banquet, toasting you as the heroes who had set things right, and before the night was out the town did something nobody would have expected of it: they voted, all together, to stop keeping secrets from one another.

The Road Back

On the road back to Wickermoor you spent a night in the barn of a kindly old follower of the Silver Path, who gave you food and shelter and asked for nothing in return.

The road had a few more stops in store. A ghost was trying in vain to gather fruit his hands could no longer hold, so you filled the basket for him; he found his rest, and left you a share of the harvest. Further on, a flock of sheep was in a panic over a {{creature:goatstealer}}, which you sent running before it could take its pick.

wm_murkwater.default:
Murkwater Bend rises out of the bayou on stilts, the largest and most lawless town in the Drowned Crossroads, built by people who came here specifically to escape the rules everywhere else in the hollow enforces. For a while, that freedom paid off handsomely, prosperity found this swamp town in a way it rarely finds towns like this, and gold flowed easily enough that people started calling their own luck a kind of magic.

They said the luck came from someone called Snake Eye Jack. But good fortune has curdled into something closer to a curse these last several years, and Murkwater's people whisper about the whole swamp being jinxed and Snake Eye Jack abandoning them. Those desperate enough still make their way into the deep mire looking for a certain shack on stilts, because in Murkwater Bend, even a cursed deal beats no deal at all.

byGroup.1:
A Withered Arm

[[SCENE_Chapter15_Adelas_Deal]]

It was Adela Druskenvald who brought you into it, appearing during the darkest hour of the night dressed in a black fur coat, a wide-brimmed hat, and long woolen gloves, an outfit so deliberately incognito that it drew more attention than it hid. She asked for a private word, and what she told you was this: a deal gone wrong with Mister Crossroads had left her arm withered and cursed, and she needed it undone before it spread any further.

She offered you money, and more besides, if you would keep it secret from Phillip. It was clear she was distraught, so you offered her a drink, which she gladly accepted, and drank more of it than you would have expected her body to handle. The next day, you even lent her a magical item that might ease her curse, a kindness not often shown to a Druskenvald.

The Bayou King

The trail led you to Murkwater Bend and its self-declared protector, Vander Boone, the Bayou King, a man who'd once turned down a deal with the Grinning Sinner and built himself a small kingdom of thugs and taxes in the swamp instead. His chief advisor, a sharp and well-connected trader named Lyla Webb, sat at his side. Before Vander would help you, or point you toward Mister Crossroads at all, he wanted to see what you were made of, and challenged you to a game of Liar's Dice at his fort.

You won. Vander took the loss with more grace than most, saying that you might have just the luck to beat someone as tricky as that goddamn crocodile. He let you rest in the fort that night, sharing food and drink and whatever he knew about the Murkwater Bend, the Drowned Crossroads, and the Grinning Sinner himself.

Screams in the Night

The rest didn't last. Piercing screams tore through the fort before dawn, Mister Crossroads' Undead thralls had scaled the walls and were already inside Murkwater Bend. Vander's own people scrambled for weapons as a blood-streaked sentry stumbled into the throne room gasping that they were over the wall, before collapsing outright. Vander gave you no room to argue. He sent you north, toward the Marshwinder Road and the sound of cursed strings playing somewhere out in the swamp, while the town itself dissolved into a fight against the shambling dead behind you.

You took the road out as instructed, leaving Murkwater Bend to its own battle, and followed the mournful wail of a steel guitar deeper into the mire, toward the Sinner's shack.

[[SCENE_Chapter15_Sinners_Shack]]

wm_rowans_rise.default:
[[SCENE_Chapter23_Rowans_Rise]]

The highest hill in the moors north of the village is crowned with a ring of standing stones so old that no one remembers who raised them. It's named for a girl called Rowan, who, as the story is told to children, grew so enchanted with the moon overhead that she climbed to the top of the hill one night and simply flew up to sit beside it, watching over Wickermoor Hollow ever after. All the search party ever found of her was a silver locket at the center of the stones, her sister's portrait inside replaced by the image of an antlered hare.

[[SCENE_Chapter23_Wickerman]]

It's a lovely story, and every part of it after "she climbed to the top of the hill" is a lie told to make something unbearable sound gentle. Rowan was the first person ever sacrificed on that hilltop, offered up the moment the Crooked Queen first stirred with enough strength to ask for one. The stones have been thirsty ever since, and the hollow's oldest, quietest fear is that they have never once stopped being fed.

[[Wickers Vigil]]

wm_crimson.default:
High in the Howlers, overlooking both the Silverbell River and the trembling town of Dawn's Gate below, stands the Crimson Monastery, stone walls, a great bell tower, and a cathedral lit always by candlelight and something else that isn't quite candlelight. Its abbot preaches purity and salvation to a flock that adores him without reservation, and to hear his sermons, the monastery is the last honest sanctuary left in a wicked hollow.

Those who decline the invitation to convert rarely get a second one. Riders and bat hounds come down from the mountainside in the dead of night, dragging the unconverted back up to the monastery's gates, and what happens behind those gates is a mystery to everyone except the people it's happened to, and they don't get the chance to talk about it afterward. The monastery calls its goddess the Crimson Rose. No one in Dawn's Gate has ever been permitted to actually see her.

byGroup.1:
[[The Crimson Monastery]]

Night of Flames

You arrived at the foot of the monastery, its red stained-glass windows seeming to watch you approach. The guards welcomed you inside without hesitation, after all, it was the Night of Flames. You could hear the chanting before you ever reached the courtyard: "Glory to the Crimson Rose, blood from the thorn, beauty from the petal!" A pyre stood at the center, ringed with unbelievers waiting their turn. One by one they repented and joined the Crimson Rose, all but one. Gareth, the very man Weston had sent you to find.

Korrin tried to talk him down, but panic and the strangeness of a voice speaking inside his own head weren't helping matters, though that same voice also told him of Melina, and that it was she who wanted Gareth to come home. Friar Olaf was already moving to light the pyre when Megumin stepped in, offering to try where Korrin hadn't succeeded. First, though, she had to win over the Crimson Abbot himself, and luck was on her side there, he'd taken a particular interest in her and let her proceed. With charm and unshakable logic, she talked Gareth into repenting and joining the Crimson Rose, if only to save his own skin. No one burned on the pyre that Night of Flames. Many new believers joined the Crimson Rose instead, or so the monastery was meant to think.

Behind the Walls

The next night was for scouting and mapping the monastery itself. Imposing as it looked from outside, it was surprisingly calm within, the halls usually silent save for the whispers of believers passing through. Some of them wore unusual features, pale skin, vacant stares, pointed ears, the occasional flash of fangs. These were what the monastery called the Bloodless, its most devoted, though notably not Friar Olaf, Houndmaster Jaeger, or Inquisitor Cromwell.

You made a friend as well. Andreas Maler, son of August Maler, saw in you a chance to change this place for the better, though he wasn't sure at first, one misstep could easily cost him his life. He took the risk anyway and shared what he'd managed to find. Inquisitor Cromwell grew suspicious too, and paid Andreas a visit of her own not long after. Quick thinking and quicker hiding kept you out of sight and off her radar.

The Dead Larder

In the Dead Larder you found believers of the Crimson Rose chained and near death from cold and exhaustion, punished for following Olaf into the sanctum and seeing something there that could not have belonged to any true goddess.

Cromwell's Trophies

Getting into Inquisitor Cromwell's room proved simple enough. What waited inside was not: a wall of hunting trophies and weapons, a slave catcher's rig among the worst of it, and a collection of jewelry that made for a fine addition to the haul.

The Belfry

The Crimson Abbot himself invited you to speak with him in the belfry, a conversation that circled purpose, loyalty, power, and what role you might play in the Crimson Rose's future. But he sensed something in you as well, anger, duplicity, lies he couldn't quite name, though he could clearly feel them all the same.

Into the Sanctum

There was no more time to wait, not if the people in the larder were to be saved. In Olaf's own chambers you found the steps needed to reach the sanctum of the Crimson Rose, and with that, you went down into the bowels of the beast.

[[SCENE_Chapter14_Viraxys]]

The Abbot Falls

Only the five of you were left standing in the blood-stained cathedral by the end. The Crimson Abbot, Marius Renathyr, vanished in sulfur and flame, his sword left standing in the altar, and with him, the power of the Crimson Rose, of Viraxys, gone from the monastery, hopefully for good.

Olaf was the first to come asking what had happened, and you brought him in quickly and laid out the plan. He agreed without much convincing, willing to do anything to save his own skin and keep his hold on power.

A Fragile Peace

Whether it would have worked is hard to say. Men like Olaf are difficult to predict, and fear of a show of power can just as easily be swallowed by greed. The same held true for Inquisitor Cromwell. She would never have beaten Olaf outright in a war between the faithful, but if someone were to inform her, catch Olaf isolated, and lend her the hounds to do it, the balance of power would tip fast. Holding the monastery in that moment was already a losing effort, the townsfolk armed and restless, the faithful who remained disoriented and unsure what had even happened. None of that mattered to Cromwell. She would find whoever killed Renathyr, and she would see them burn.

wm_dawns_gate.default:
Dawn's Gate sits where the moors give way to the foothills of the Howlers, a hunting and mining town that has survived on the mountain's resources for generations. It should, by rights, be one of the more peaceful corners of the hollow, it is instead one of the most frightened, living every night in the shadow of the monastery that looms directly above it.

[[SCENE_Chapter14_Environment]]

The riders come without warning, baying hounds and torchlight cutting down the mountainside toward whoever the monastery has decided needs saving from themselves. Families keep their doors barred and their opinions about the Crimson Faith carefully unspoken, because in Dawn's Gate, the difference between a devout neighbor and an informant is impossible to know until it's already cost you someone.

byGroup.1:
A Familiar Face

You arrived that morning to a commotion in the town square. Someone was addressing a crowd, though you only caught the tail end of it before the speaker leapt down and was already halfway out of town. The figure looked like Sylas, or near enough to pass for him. Megumin stopped him, trying to understand who or what he is, he spared a few words for Megumin, but as if finishing a monologue and leaving the stage, he quickly snuck past Megumin. She tried to stop him using a spell, but sadly it backfired, with the spell giving him the cover to slip out of your reach.

The Briar Public House

Your path led you to the Briar Public House, where Sylas was busy making, or perhaps leveraging, a friendship with Kristoff Gruber, one that paid Kristoff handsomely for his trouble. Whether that investment ever pays off in kind remains to be seen.

Tharn met Tabitha Druckeryn at the bar, a seamstress who wanted more out of life than the town seemed willing to give her. She'd hoped for at least a proper goodbye before you moved on, and didn't get one. Perhaps their paths will cross again before this is all over.

Korrin and Webrin found their own connection that night, to the same man, though for very different reasons. August Maler, illuminator and father of Andreas Maler, drew Korrin in for his skill and knowledge, the kind of mind worth learning from. Webrin saw something else entirely in him. Whether her webbed heart beat any faster holding his hand is hers to say, but two widowers finding each other in a town like Dawn's Gate is the kind of thread that has a way of pulling tighter over time.

wm_webwoods.default:
The Webwoods hold up to their name well enough on their own. Silk drapes over branch and bramble the moment the road bends south of it, and the farther you veer from the path, the thicker it grows, strand over strand, until it's less a forest and more a single vast, patient structure that happens to have trees growing through it. Every step further in comes with the sense of something testing the ground first.

Spiders here run larger than they have any right to, and there are more of them the deeper you go. Some travelers who've made it out swear the trees themselves shift position after dark, roots pulling free and settling somewhere new by morning, though no one's ever caught one moving, only ever the difference between where a tree stood at dusk and where it stands at dawn.

wm_maidenmist.default:
South of the village, the hills roll on for miles into fog and headstones, Maidenmist Cemetery, final resting place for every soul the hollow has ever lost, for longer than anyone can account for. It has always been there, as far as anyone knows; no records mark its founding, and the wrought iron fence that rings it is said, by the people who live closest to it, to creep a little further outward every single night.

[[SCENE_Chapter19_Maidenmist_Cemetery]]

There is truth under that superstition. The cemetery sits atop a tear in the Shroud itself, a wound that lets the valley's dead rest properly on one side and lets something considerably less peaceful claw at the seam from the other. A lone gravedigger has kept that seam closed for longer than any single soul should have to carry a burden like that, alone, in the fog, with the gate creeping a little closer to the village with every night that he manages to hold the line.

[[Maidenmist Cemetery]]

wm_silverbell.default: Every road in Wickermoor Hollow eventually touches the Silverbell, the river that threads the whole valley together, rising somewhere out past the Drowned Crossroads, curling past the village that grew up along its banks specifically because of it, and finally emptying its whole silvered length into the wide grey reach of Moonsong Lake.

wm_ghostlight_express.default:
The Ghostlight Express is no ordinary train. It carries the newly dead through the Shroud toward Druskenvald, offering the departed one final journey before whatever waits for them on the other side, and on the rarest occasions, it grants passage to the living too. It manifests wherever it's needed, always at the dead of the night, most often near graveyards or standing stones, and once boarded, there's no getting off until it reaches wherever it's decided you need to go.

byGroup.1:
[[The Ghostlight Express]]

All Aboard

A train stop in the middle of nowhere. A puppet, a tree, a bird, and a devil, all drawn to it. Little did they know a spider would join them in time as well.

Fog surrounded you, thick enough that only a single fiddle managed to cut through it. Then came a train whistle, and a ghostly blue light, and the train itself, stopping right in front of you. A frogman stepped down from it and asked for your tickets. For two of you, this was the first time your eyes had ever opened in this world. For the other two, it was every bit as strange as it was for you. You boarded anyway. The train had to stay on schedule, and as long as you held a ticket, you were always welcome aboard the Ghostlight Express.

The Trainhopper

Inside, you were ambushed by a trainhopper, one that shattered a window and let the wailing Shroud pour in, twisting one of the ghostly passengers into something monstrous. You prevailed, though it's hard to say what might have become of your own souls if you hadn't.

Unfinished Business

The frogman asked for your help after that, calming the other spirits aboard, souls too tangled in unfinished business to move on. Along the way, Megumin crossed paths with a gramophone playing a song like nothing you'd heard before, and you found a pair of curious string marionettes tucked away in the cars. One by one, you helped them all: the Daydreamer, the Sweetheart, the Mariner, the Harlequin, the Jailbird, and the Songstress, each of them finally free to move on because of you.

Lord and Lady Druskenvald

The ghosts weren't the only passengers aboard. Lord and Lady Druskenvald were traveling the train as well, cheerful company by any measure, especially Adela, who offered to read your fortunes. Whether you put any stock in divination is another matter entirely.

Derailed

Belief in fortune-telling or not, something far more powerful than fate had decided to derail the train, throwing you out into a forest watched over by the Crooked Moon. You remember the rest from there. The Ghostlight Express woke to a corrupted life of its own and tried to feed your souls into its boiler, but the train was defeated in the end, its corruption cleansed. You four, along with Phillip and Adela, were left stranded in the middle of nowhere, with nothing but the frogman's promise that he'd return once the train was fixed.

A Little Respite

Whether the Ghostlight Express was a savior or something else entirely is hard to say, but after everything in Kalero, you were glad for the chance to breathe. It all still felt like a haze, but you'd done good there, whatever it cost you. You even managed to close your eyes for a while in the sleeping wagon, though the dreams that found you there weren't restful for everyone, closer to nightmares for some. You knew of this train. You never imagined you'd actually ride it.

All Aboard

A crossroads, standing stones, and fog, a place of power if there ever was one. All of you were drawn to it, and one by one, you arrived. Distrust and wariness passed between you, warranted enough, strangers with no reason yet to trust one another, no answer for who the others were or why they'd been called here too. The fog around you thickened with every passing minute, until only a single fiddle managed to cut through it. Unusual as it was, even by the standards of some of you, you had tickets in hand, and understood, somehow, that this was exactly why you'd been drawn here. You boarded. gnarlborn.name: Gnarlborn
gnarlborn.body:
Gnarlborn are a tree-like species native to Ardengloom, usually sprouting up from the soil of the twisted, dark forest. Their home is forever haunted by the souls of long-dead Fey, which inhabit the enormous, face-bearing trees known as Elderwoods. These folk commune with these beings to receive primordial wisdom.

Resembling gnarled trees with glowing faces hollowed into the bark, their individual patterns of branches, moss, and lichen can result in a wide diversity of appearances. Most gnarlborn live for over 500 years, but those with the strongest connection to the Elderwoods have been said to live to be thousands of years old.

azureborn.name: Azureborn
azureborn.body:
Azureborn are a harpy-like species native to Astramar, often materializing from the bright blue night sky filled with twinkling stars and winds of arcane power. Bearing a connection to the aither that courses through the air and land of the province, they are an inherently prescient folk that can divine the future by looking to the cosmos. They have built a society of magical wonder through grand vision, endless curiosity, and dedication to study.

Sprouting feathers across their entire body and wings attached to each of their arms, this diverse folk can resemble all manner of avian creatures, from raptors with earthy tones to tropical birds of vibrant and colorful plumage. They typically live 100 years, although many of the wisest among them have lived up to 400.

plagueborn.name: Plagueborn
plagueborn.body:
Plagueborn are a rat-like species native to Bubonia, typically coalescing in the pestilent haze that hangs over the province. They are deeply connected to the virulent and deadly plague that afflicts and shapes their society, which persists through cunning, ruthlessness, and the sheer will to live. They are the most adaptable species of Druskenvald, quickly discovering the means to survive even the harshest environments.

Appearing as large plague rats with humanoid physiology, their short fur ranges from grays and browns to various shades of green. They bear jagged teeth and claws that all carry a strain of plague to which they are immune but can prove deadly to others. Their nimble tails can vary greatly in length and thickness, often reflecting their family, clan, or guild. Plagueborn usually live no longer than 100 years.

ashborn.name: Ashborn
ashborn.body:
Ashborn are an imp-like species native to Chernabos, typically coalescing from the sulfuric ash of the province's hellfire and brimstone volcanoes. Infused with the fiendish power of the Hells, this folk has managed to survive and even prosper in the barrens and badlands of the province through guile, boldness, and industriousness. Said to be favored by fortune itself, ashborn count on luck to twist the balance in the most dire of situations.

Their short stature ranges from slight to stout, but this makes them no less dangerous, for each ashborn has a venomous tail resembling a scorpion's, always ready to strike. They sport horns and skin tones in varying shades of red and gray that reflect their devilish origin, and they typically live 100 years.

curseborn.name: Curseborn
curseborn.body:
Curseborn are a werewolf-like species native to Edwardia, often emerging from the dense, cursed fog that rolls across the province. Sharing a strong connection to a malediction called the Grey, which demands balance at the threat of certain doom, they have managed to build a civilization of advancement and progress, countered by rampant strife, pollution, and hunger.

Covered head to toe with thick fur and bearing sharp teeth and claws, this lupine species evokes the hallmarks and appearance of wolves but with clearly humanoid physiology. If not brought to an early grave by the Grey, they typically live for up to 100 years, although technological advancement has led to certain individuals approaching 200 years old.

harvestborn.name: Harvestborn
harvestborn.body:
Harvestborn are a scarecrow-like species native to Enoch, most often crafted with great care by Methuselah, the lord of the province. Infused with the vital, green magic that surges through the immensely fertile land, they have a strong connection to the cycle of both the harvest and life, death, and rebirth. They feed much of Druskenvald with the crops they grow in a relatively peaceful society that puts a focus on community, family, and fellowship.

As a constructed species resembling any manner of scarecrow, their bodies are comprised of a mixture of wood, metal, straw, and other implements. Their glowing-eyed heads might be made from a burlap sack or a crop such as a pumpkin or turnip. Staying true to the cycle, they generally live 100 years before accepting the next step of death and becoming reborn once more.

relicborn.name: Relicborn
relicborn.body:
Relicborn are a skeleton-like species native to Kalero, generally emerging from the numerous tombs and crypts that line the canyon walls of the province. They thrive in a culture of celebration and remembrance, which infuses the very essence of every member of the species. Dancing between the energy of a vivacious party and the serenity of peaceful reflection, this folk holds a deep appreciation for both the living and the dead.

They appear as skeletons decorated with a wide array of vibrant colors, patterns, and styles, and their bones are encased in a translucent, glowing substance that provides them with a similar mass and shape to other humanoid species, allowing them to comfortably wear clothing and armor. Some relicborn can even grow hair from their skulls, which is often shaped into bombastic styles. Relicborn typically live for 250 years before losing their form and collapsing into a pile of bones.

silkborn.name: Silkborn
silkborn.body:
Silkborn are a spider-like species native to Nerukhet, typically emerging from silken cocoons amidst thick webbing that fills miles of tunnels throughout the subterranean province. They have a deep kinship and connection with the bejeweled arachnids and insects that have assisted them in building the grandest civilization in Druskenvald. This folk also channels the great gems that fill the caverns of the province with light and power, bringing them ever closer to the gods that spared their kind from an ancient calamity.

While this species has humanoid proportions, they have arachnid features — hardened carapace skin, numerous eyes, segmented limbs that grow from their backs, and mandibles that sprout from their mouths. They generally live for 250 years, but those at the higher echelons of their civilizations have been known to live nearly 800 years.

deepborn.name: Deepborn
deepborn.body:
Deepborn are a fish-like species native to Olmarsh, typically rising up from the abyssal depths of the province's black sea — home to terrors beyond imagining known as the Hungry Ones. Immersed in a near-constant eldritch presence that emerges from the deep and descends from beyond the stars, these folk manage their state of paranoia by embracing and harnessing the uncanny and cosmic.

While they are primarily piscine in their anatomy, they can possess features found in a wide variety of sea creatures, including cephalopods and crustaceans. They typically live for around 150 years, but certain members of occult orders have been known to live for 600 years.

stoneborn.name: Stoneborn
stoneborn.body:
Stoneborn are a gargoyle-like species native to Pholsense, usually meticulously carved by the lord of the province, Archbishop Danton Alexandre Renault. Blessed by the divine power known as the Silver Path, these people can call upon the godliness that suffuses their construction. In a domain of darkness, they have looked to the light of their god to build a civilization that attempts to uphold what is good and lawful at all costs.

Their stony skin matches the same hue and pattern as the stone they were carved from. While all of their kind have broad wings that carry their dense, heavy bodies, their biology can evoke a wide variety of creatures — including bats, fiends, dragons, birds, angels, dogs, and lizards — often combining features into a chimeric blend. They usually live for 300 years before crumbling into rubble.

threadborn.name: Threadborn
threadborn.body:
Threadborn are a doll-like species native to Picco, most often built with love by Blinski II, the master toymaker and lord of the province. In a land that is mostly fabricated and constructed to maximize the fun of all who live there, the essence of joy, thrill, and friendship are woven into a threadborn's very nature. They cherish the bonds made between loved ones and always maintain a childlike wonder and whimsy, no matter one's age.

As living dolls, these folk are constructed with a variety of materials, including cloth, wood, metal, porcelain, stuffing, yarn, and anything else a toy might be made of. With the most varied body shapes of all Druskenvald's species, each threadborn represents a unique representation of fun. They usually live for 100 years before falling apart and needing to be rebuilt.

graveborn.name: Graveborn
graveborn.body:
Graveborn are a ghoul-like species native to Syndramas, typically rising from one of the countless graves that mark the frozen battlefields of the province. They were first created in a kingdom-wide ritual that twisted countless humans into new Undead creatures that barely resembled who they once were. Graveborn now wage war endlessly and perpetuate a culture of martial prowess, relentlessness, and grave honor. These people are infused with the necrotic and draconic essence of the powerful drakkonite metal found throughout the province, which has given them a strange taste for spoiled flesh of any variety.

Appearing as the corpses of twisted humanoids, graveborn have powerful snouts and jaws with elongated teeth and tongues that assist in the devouring of flesh and bone. Their physiology is sturdy, as if magically designed to be perfected for war. If not killed in war, as befalls many of their kind, they can live up to 300 years before decaying away.

bogborn.name: Bogborn
bogborn.body:
Bogborn are a troll-like species native to Zulrogg, usually rising from the still, dark waters of the swampy province. From the moment of rebirth, they have a symbiotic relationship with the flora and fauna of the wild — and often treacherous — mire. Their ability to survive is further enhanced by the naturally regenerative biology often found in trolls.

Towering over most, these hearty folk can face any trial of nature, and they often utilize their athleticism in pursuits of hunting and survival. Bearing prominent noses and tusks, their tough hides are generally shades of green or blue. Bogborn typically live 100 years before moving on to the spirit world.

wm_horned_king.text: Don't sign anything a stranger offers you after dark. Not even if he already knows your name. Especially then.
wm_horned_king.source: an old woman at the Founder's Round

wm_crooked_queen.text: The old stories say this valley had a queen before it ever had a name. The old stories also say to stop asking about her.

wm_beast_of_blight.text: Something in the old Greenwood is still grieving. You can hear it when the wind turns rotten.
wm_beast_of_blight.source: a woodcutter at the forest's edge

wm_weeping_widow.text: Some nights a woman's weeping drifts across the lake. The boatmen row faster, and they never look back.

wm_chained_reaper.text: Out past the cemetery something drags a great stone behind it. Some nights you can hear the chain. Some nights it just sounds tired.

wm_grinning_sinner.text: Luck's for sale down in the bayou, if you know which shack to knock on. Nobody's ever been happy with the price.
wm_grinning_sinner.source: a card sharp in Murkwater Bend

wm_harvest_terror.text: The fields used to sing at harvest time. Now nobody walks the rows after sundown, and even the crows won't land.

wm_crimson_abbot.text: The monastery's master is the kindest man you'll ever meet. Everyone says so. Everyone who came back, anyway.

wm_rowans_rise.text: A girl once climbed the stone hill to sit beside the moon. On clear nights, the children still leave her a candle up there.

wm_skitterdeep.text: They called it Glitterdeep, once. Put your ear to the old shaft and you'll hear why nobody does anymore.

wm_maidenmist.text: Count the fence posts at Maidenmist on your way in, and again on your way out. You'll never get the same number twice.

wm_webwoods.text: If the road south feels sticky underfoot, turn back. If it feels like it's moving, run.

wm_dawns_gate.text: In Dawn's Gate they bar their doors at dusk and pray toward the mountain. Ask them what they fear more, the dark or the bells, and they won't answer.

wm_crimson.text: High in the Howlers there's a cathedral where the candles never go out. The light through its windows is the wrong shade of red.

wm_moonsong.text: It rains on Moonsong Lake more than anywhere in the hollow. The fishermen say it's the lake weeping, and you shouldn't fish where it weeps.

wm_howlers.text: The wind in the Howlers never stops. Listen long enough and you'll swear it's calling a name. Don't answer it.

wm_hartsblight.text: The Greenwood went the colour of a bruise in a single season. Whatever's in the air there, don't breathe it, and don't bring any home.

wm_wytchwood.text: There's no road into the Wytchwood. There used to be one out of it.
wm_wytchwood.source: the old granny who sweeps the square

wm_drowned.text: Down where the black waters meet, luck used to come cheap. Now it just comes strange, and it follows you home.
wm_drowned.source: a gambler down on his luck

wm_murkwater.text: Murkwater Bend's got no laws, only a king and his taxes. Pay both and you'll sleep fine. Mostly.

wm_village.text: Every face carved into the old oak belonged to somebody once. Nobody can tell you who carves the new ones.

wm_foxwillow.text: The best bread in the hollow comes out of Foxwillow. Lately it tastes of smoke.

wm_silverbell.text: Every road in the hollow reaches the Silverbell sooner or later. So does everything that falls into it.

wm_memorys_rest.text: They'll help you forget whatever hurts, at Memory's Rest. They're very good at it. Too good, some say.

wm_ghostlight_express.text: If you hear a train whistle where there are no tracks, stand very still. It isn't your stop. Not yet.
